narrations.arabic: وكانت شريعة عيسى عليه السلام انه بعث بالتوحيد والاخلاص وبما أوصى به نوح وإبراهيم وموسى عليهم السلام وأنزل عليه الانجيل وأخذ عليه الميثاق الذي أخذ على النبيين وشرع له في الكتاب اقام الصلاة مع الدين والأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر وتحريم الحرام وتحليل الحلال وانزل عليه في الانجيل مواعظ وامثال وليس فيها قصاص ولا أحكام حدود ولا فرض مواريث وانزل عليه تخفيف ما كان على موسى عليه السلام في التوراة وهو قول قول عز وجل في الذي قال عيسى بن مريم لبني اسرائيل ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرّم عليكم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: The law of Jesus: he was sent with monotheism and sincerity and with what Noah, Abraham and Moses were charged with. The Evangel was sent down to him, and in it a lightening of what had lain upon Moses in the Torah. That is His word, 'to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden you.'

note.en: Tabrisi: Jesus says this as an argument against the Christians who call the Messiah God's son. Do not ascribe me to Him; I am His servant as you are His servants [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أي: لما سمع ورأى أنهم يكفرون، والحواس الخمس التي قدرها الله في الناس السمع للصوت، والبصر للألوان وتمييزها، والشم لمعرفة الروائح الطيبة والخبيثة، والذوق للطعوم وتمييزها، واللمس لمعرفة الحار والبارد واللين والخشن.
narrations.chain: Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: 'When Jesus sensed their faithlessness' means when he heard and saw that they were disbelieving. The five senses God appointed in people are hearing for sound, sight for colors and telling them apart, smell for good and foul odors, taste for flavors, and touch for hot and cold, soft and rough.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: اما عند الناس فانهم سمّوا حواريين لأنهم كانوا قصَّارين يخلصون الثياب من الوسخ بالغسل وهو اسم مشتق من الخبز الحوار واما عندنا فسمي الحواريون الحواريين لأنهم كانوا مخلصين في أنفسهم ومخلصين غيرهم من أوساخ الذنوب بالوعظ والتذكير.

text.en: Among the people they were called hawariyyun because they were bleachers who cleansed clothes of dirt by washing. But with us they were called hawariyyun because they were purified in themselves and purified others of the filth of sins by exhortation and reminder.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: نحن هم، نشهد للرسل على أممها

text.en: On 'so write us among the witnesses': We are they. We bear witness for the messengers against their communities.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: سألت الرضا (عليه السلام) عن قوله: { وَمَكَرُواْ وَمَكَرَ ٱللَّهُ }. فقال: " إن الله تبارك و تعالى لا يمكر، و لكنه عز و جل يجازيهم جزاء المكر
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Muadhi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Said al-Kufi al-Hamdani, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from his father

text.en: I asked al-Rida about His word, 'Then they plotted, and Allah also devised.' He said: 'God, Blessed and Exalted, does not plot; rather He requites them with the recompense of plotting.'

perspectives.en: Tabrisi and Tusi both report from al-Baqir that 'above the world's women' means the women of her own age, since Fatimah is the mistress of the women of the worlds [2][9]. Tusi adds that Mary was not a prophetess, and that the angels' address to her may be counted a miracle and an honor, for signs may appear at the hands of the friends of God and the righteous [9]. Qurtubi holds the reverse on both counts: the sound view is that Mary was a prophetess, since God revealed to her through the angel as He did to the other prophets, and so she is superior to all women, first and last, with Fatimah after her [56].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فاصطفائها تقبلها لعبادة الله وتطهيرها اعتصامها بعصمة الله فهي مصطفاة معصومة

sources.gloss: Her being chosen is His accepting her for the worship of God, and her purification is her being held within God's protection; so she is chosen and preserved from sin.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي على نساء عالمي زمانك لأن فاطمة بنت رسول الله صلّى الله عليها وعلى أبيها وبعلـها وبنيها سيدة نساء العالمين وهو قول أبي جعفر ع

sources.gloss: That is, over the women of your own age, because Fatimah daughter of the Messenger of God is the mistress of the women of the worlds; and this is the statement of Abu Jafar.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يشاهد هذه القصص ولا قرأها من الكتب ولا تعلّمها إذ كان نشؤه بين أهل مكة ولم يكونوا أهل كتاب فوضح الله أن أوحى إليه بها وفي ذلك صحة نبوته

sources.gloss: The Prophet did not witness these accounts, nor read them in books, nor learn them, for he grew up among the people of Mecca and they were not a people of scripture; so God made clear that He revealed them to him, and in that is the soundness of his prophethood.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أحدهما: أنه المسيح سمّاه كلمة عن ابن عباس وقتادة وجماعة من المفسرين وإنما سمي بذلك لأنه كان بكلمة من الله من غير والد

sources.gloss: The first view is that the Messiah is what is named a Word, from Ibn Abbas, Qatada and a group of the exegetes; he was so named because he came to be by a word from God, with no father.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لم تقل ذلك استبعاداً واستنكارا بل إنما قالت استفهاماً واستعظاماً لقدرة الله لأن في طبع البشر التعجب مما خرج عن المعتاد

sources.gloss: She did not say it out of disbelief or denial, but as a question and in awe of God's power, for it is in human nature to marvel at what departs from the customary.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وإنما قال ذلك ليكون حجة على النصارى في قولـهم المسيح ابن الله والمعنى لا تنسبوني إليه فأنا عبده كما أنكم عبيد لـه

sources.gloss: He said this so that it would be an argument against the Christians in their saying that the Messiah is the son of God; the sense is: do not ascribe me to Him, for I am His servant just as you are His servants.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أحدها: أن معناه من أعواني على هؤلاء الكفار مع معونة الله عن السدي وابن جريج والثاني: أن معناه من أنصاري في السبيل إلى الله عن الحسن

sources.gloss: The first: it means who will help me against these unbelievers together with the help of God, from al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj. The second: it means who are my helpers on the path to God, from al-Hasan.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ويجوز عندنا أن يكون ذلك معجزة لها وكرامة، وإن لم تكن نبية لأن اظهار المعجزات - عندنا - تجوز على يد الأولياء، والصالحين

sources.gloss: It is permissible in our view that this was a miracle and an honor for her, even though she was not a prophetess, because in our view the showing of miracles is permitted at the hands of the friends of God and the righteous.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإنما قدم ذكر السجود في الآية على الركوع، لأن النية به التأخير والتقدير اركعي واسجدي، لأن الواو لا توجب الترتيب

sources.gloss: Prostration was mentioned before bowing in the verse although the intent is that it comes later, the sense being bow and prostrate, because 'and' does not impose an order.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإنما قيد قوله: { فيكون طيراً بأذن الله } ولم يقيد قوله: { أخلق من الطين كهيئة الطير } بذكر إذن الله لينبه بذكر الاذن أنه من فعل الله دون عيسى

sources.gloss: He qualified 'and it will become a bird by Allah's leave' and did not qualify 'I will create for you the form of a bird out of clay' with the mention of God's leave, so as to signal by that mention that it is God's act and not Jesus'.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فانما أحل لهم لحوم الابل والثروب وأشياء من الطير والحيتان، مما كان محرماً في شرع موسى (ع) ولم يحل لهم جميع ما كان محرماً عليهم من الظلم، والغصب، والكذب، والعبث وغير ذلك

sources.gloss: He made lawful for them the meat of camels, fat, and some birds and fish that had been forbidden in the law of Moses; He did not make lawful for them all that had been forbidden them of injustice, seizure, lying, frivolity and the like.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أي: لما سمع ورأى أنهم يكفرون، والحواس الخمس التي قدرها الله في الناس السمع للصوت، والبصر للألوان وتمييزها، والشم لمعرفة الروائح الطيبة والخبيثة، والذوق للطعوم وتمييزها، واللمس لمعرفة الحار والبارد واللين والخشن.

sources.gloss: That is, when he heard and saw that they were disbelieving. The five senses God appointed in people: hearing for sound, sight for colors and telling them apart, smell for good and foul odors, taste for flavors and telling them apart, and touch for hot and cold, soft and rough.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أول من سوهم عليه مريم بنت عمران، و هو قول الله عز و جل: { وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يُلْقُون أَقْلاَمَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ } و السهام ستة

sources.gloss: The first person over whom lots were cast was Mary daughter of Imran, and that is the word of God, 'when they were casting lots to see which of them would take charge of Mary's care'; and the lots were six.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قالوا: ما نرى الذي تصنع إلا سحرا فأرنا آية نعلم أنك صادق؟ قال: أرأيتم إن أخبرتكم بما تأكلون و ما تدخرون في بيوتكم، يقول: ما أكلتم في بيوتكم قبل أن تخرجوا، و ما ادخرتم إلى الليل، تعلمون أني صادق؟ قالوا: نعم.

sources.gloss: They said: we see what you do as nothing but sorcery, so show us a sign by which we may know you are truthful. He said: if I tell you what you eat and what you store in your houses, that is, what you ate in your houses before you came out and what you put away for the night, will you know that I am truthful? They said yes.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نحن هم، نشهد للرسل على أممها

sources.gloss: We are they; we bear witness for the messengers against their communities.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله تبارك و تعالى لا يمكر، و لكنه عز و جل يجازيهم جزاء المكر

sources.gloss: God, Blessed and Exalted, does not plot; rather He requites them with the recompense of plotting.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: كلّمُوها شفاهاً لأنها كانت محدّثة تحدّثهم ويحدّثونها

sources.gloss: They spoke to her face to face, for she was muhaddatha: she would speak with them and they would speak with her.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: فقالوا ان مريم كانت سيدة نساء عالمها وان الله عز وجل جعلك سيدة نساء عالمك وعالمها وسيدة نساء الأولين والآخرين.

sources.gloss: They said: Mary was the mistress of the women of her world, and God has made you the mistress of the women of your world and of hers, and the mistress of the women of the first and the last.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وانزل عليه تخفيف ما كان على موسى عليه السلام في التوراة وهو قول قول عز وجل في الذي قال عيسى بن مريم لبني اسرائيل ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرّم عليكم

sources.gloss: And there was sent down to him a lightening of what had lain upon Moses in the Torah, and that is the word of God concerning what Jesus son of Mary said to the Children of Israel, 'and to make lawful for you some of the things that were forbidden you'.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: واما عندنا فسمي الحواريون الحواريين لأنهم كانوا مخلصين في أنفسهم ومخلصين غيرهم من أوساخ الذنوب بالوعظ والتذكير.

sources.gloss: With us the disciples were called hawariyyun because they were purified in themselves and purified others of the filth of sins by exhortation and reminder.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: فظاهر القرآن والأحاديث يقتضي أن مريم أفضل من جميع نساء العالم من حوّاء إلى آخر ٱمرأة تقوم عليها الساعة فإن الملائكة قد بلغتها الوحي عن الله عز وجل بالتكليف والإخبار والبشارة كما بلغت سائر الأنبياء فهي إذاً نبيّة والنبيّ أفضل من الوليّ فهي أفضل من كل النساء: الأوّلين والآخرين مطلقاً. ثم بعدها في الفضيلة فاطمة ثم خديجة ثم آسِية

sources.gloss: The apparent sense of the Quran and the reports requires that Mary is superior to all the women of the world, from Eve to the last woman upon whom the Hour will come, for the angels conveyed revelation to her from God with charge, report and glad tidings as they conveyed it to the rest of the prophets, so she is a prophetess, and a prophet is superior to a friend of God, so she is superior to all women, the first and the last, absolutely; and after her in excellence is Fatimah, then Khadija, then Asiya.

essay.en:
The passage opens with God speaking to Jesus directly, straight after the plotting of the verse before: 'O Jesus, I shall take you[r soul], and I shall raise you up toward Myself.' What the taking means is the oldest question in these verses. Al-Tusi reports three readings: that God took him up from the earth to the heaven with no death at all; that it was a taking in sleep; and that the clauses are inverted, the taking coming after the raising [7]. Al-Tabrisi gives the grammarians' reason for the last of these, that the conjunction imposes no order [3]. Setting those who followed Jesus above the faithless, al-Tusi adds, may be ascendancy by proof and argument, or by might and victory [7].

Verses 56 and 57 open out the judgement just promised: al-Tusi reads them as the detail of the summary 'I will judge between you' [8][9]. The punishment in this world he glosses as abasement by killing, captivity and the jizya, with the punishment of the hereafter unending [8]; and al-Tabrisi finds in the promise to pay the faithful in full an argument against those who hold that deeds can be cancelled [4]. 'These that We recite to you' gathers up the whole telling: the reports of Jesus, Zechariah, John, the disciples and the Jews of the Children of Israel [10].

Then the argument itself. The case of Jesus is the case of Adam, and al-Tusi observes that the comparison holds all the more, since Adam came from neither male nor female [11]. The occasion, al-Tabrisi reports, was the delegation of Najran, whose chiefs asked the Prophet whether he had ever seen a child born without a father [5]. When the answer did not settle them, verse 61 turned the dispute into a mutual imprecation. Tabatabai records that the commentators are unanimous, the narrations agree and history confirms it: nobody came out with the Prophet but Ali, Fatimah and the two grandsons [2]. The Christians drew back and asked for terms [5]. What is left is the true account, one God, and a warning for whoever turns away.

note.en: Fayd Kashani glosses 'I shall take you' as completing your term and shielding you from their killing, and 'raise you up toward Myself' as to the place of My honour and the abode of My angels [21].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إنه ما شبه أمر أحد من أنبياء الله و حججه للناس إلا أمر عيسى (عليه السلام) وحده، لأنه رفع من الأرض حيا و قبض روحه بين السماء و الأرض، ثم رفع إلى السماء و رد عليه روحه
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sad ibn Uqda al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhdhal, from his father, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa

text.en: The affair of none of God's prophets and proofs was made ambiguous to people except the affair of Jesus alone, for he was raised from the earth alive, his soul taken between the heaven and the earth, then he was raised to the heaven and his soul returned to him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن عيسى (عليه السلام) وعد أصحابه ليلة رفعه الله إليه فاجتمعوا إليه عند المساء، و هم اثنا عشر رجلا … إن الله أوحى إلي أنه رافعي إليه الساعة، و مطهري من اليهود، فأيكم يلقى عليه شبحي فيقتل، و يصلب، و يكون معي في درجتي؟
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Humran ibn Ayan, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Jesus made an appointment with his companions the night God raised him; twelve men gathered at evening … God has revealed to me that He is raising me to Him this hour and purifying me from the Jews. Which of you will have my likeness cast on him, be killed and crucified, and be with me in my rank?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: رفع عيسى بن مريم (عليه السلام) بمدرعة صوف من غزل مريم، و من نسج مريم، و من خياطة مريم، فلما انتهى إلى السماء نودي: يا عيسى، ألق عنك زينة الدنيا
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ibn Umar, from one of our companions, from a man who narrated it to him, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Jesus son of Mary was raised in a woolen cloak of Mary's spinning, Mary's weaving and Mary's sewing. When he reached the heaven, he was called: O Jesus, cast off from yourself the adornment of the world.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فلما فرغوا دنوا من رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)، فقالوا له: إلى ما تدعونا؟ فقال: إلى شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، و أني رسول الله، و أن عيسى عبد مخلوق، يأكل و يشرب و يحدث … قالوا: فمن أبوه؟
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When they had finished they came near the Messenger of God and said: To what do you call us? He said: To testifying that there is no god but God, that I am God's Messenger, and that Jesus is a created servant who eats, drinks and relieves himself. They said: Then who is his father?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: فَأَبْرَزَ النَّبِيُ‏ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ عَلِيّاً وَالْحَسَنَ وَالْحُسَيْنَ وَفَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلاَمُ وَقَرَنَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ بِنَفْسِهِ … إِنَّمَا عَنَى بِهَا عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhawayh al-Muaddib and Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Jafar al-Himyari, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt

text.en: The Prophet brought forward Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and Fatimah, and joined their souls to his own … By 'ourselves' He meant Ali ibn Abi Talib.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Hasan
narrations.arabic: فأخرج رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) من الأنفس معه أبي، و من البنين أنا و أخي، و من النساء فاطمة أمي من الناس جميعا، فنحن أهله و لحمه و دمه و نفسه، و نحن منه و هو منا
narrations.chain: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hamdani, from Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim ibn Qays al-Ashari, from Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his uncle al-Hasan

text.en: The Messenger of God brought out, from the souls, my father with him; from the sons, myself and my brother; and from the women, Fatimah my mother, out of all the people. So we are his family, his flesh, his blood and his soul; we are from him and he is from us.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ان نفسي نفس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله والنساء فاطمة عليها السلام والابناء الحسن والحسين. ثم ندم القوم فسألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله الاعفاء فأعفاهم
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan, from Bakr ibn Abdillah ibn Habib, from Tamim ibn Buhlul, from Sulayman ibn Hakim, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Makhul, from Ali ibn Abi Talib

text.en: My soul is the soul of the Messenger of God; the women is Fatimah; and the sons are al-Hasan and al-Husayn. Then the people regretted it and asked the Messenger of God to excuse them, and he excused them.

note.en: Al-Tabrisi reports a reading that names the disputants themselves: God knows they will not go through with the imprecation, because they recognize the Prophet's prophethood [6].

perspectives.en: Both traditions read verse 61 as the mubahala with the delegation of Najran [5][37]. Al-Razi takes it as the last step of the argument: once the proofs are clear, break off the discussion and treat the obstinate as obstinate, by calling them to mutual cursing [45]. Qurtubi treats the episode as a mark of the Prophet's standing, since they refused it and accepted the jizya, and reads 'our sons' as evidence that a daughter's children are called sons [37]. The Shia blocks press further: al-Tusi records that his companions argued from 'our souls' that Ali was the most excellent of the companions [13].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وقد أطبق المفسرون واتفقت الرواية وأيده التاريخ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم حضر للمباهلة ولم يحضر معه إلاَّ علي وفاطمة والحسنان عليهم السلام

sources.gloss: The commentators are unanimous, the narrations agree and history supports it that the Messenger of God came out for the mubahala and none came with him but Ali, Fatimah and the two grandsons.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فأما النحويون فيقولون هو على التقديم والتأخير إني رافعك ومتوفيك لأن الواو لا توجب الترتيب

sources.gloss: As for the grammarians, they say it is a case of inversion: I am raising you and taking you, because the conjunction does not impose order.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهذه الآية حجة على من قال بالإحباط لأنه سبحانه وعد بتوفية الأجر وهو الثواب والتوفية منافية للإحباط

sources.gloss: This verse is a proof against whoever holds that deeds are cancelled, since God promised the full payment of the reward, and full payment is incompatible with cancellation.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل نزلت الآيات في وفد نجران العاقب والسيد ومن معهما قالوا لرسول الله هل رأيت ولداً من غير ذكر

sources.gloss: It is said the verses came down about the delegation of Najran, al-Aqib and al-Sayyid and those with them, who said to the Messenger of God: have you ever seen a child born without a male?

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل معناه إنه عليم بهؤلاء المجادلين بغير حق وبأنهم لا يقدمون على مباهلتك لمعرفتهم بنبوتك

sources.gloss: It is said the meaning is that He knows these men who dispute without right, and that they will not go forward with your mubahala, because they recognize your prophethood.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أحدها - قابضك برفعك من الارض إلى السماء من غير وفاة موت في قول الحسن وابن جريج وابن زيد. الثاني - متوفيك وفاة نوم في قول ابن عباس ووهب ابن منية. والثالث - ان فيه تقديماً وتأخيراً، ومعناه إني رافعك، ومتوفيك فيما بعد ذكره الفراء

sources.gloss: The first: taking you by raising you from the earth to the heaven with no death by dying, in the view of al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd. The second: taking you in sleep, in the view of Ibn Abbas and Wahb ibn Munabbih. The third: that there is inversion here, the sense being, I am raising you and taking you afterwards, which al-Farra mentioned.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معنى قوله { فأما } تفصيل المجمل … فعذابهم في الدنيا اذلالهم بالقتل، والأسر، والسبي، والخسف، والجزية، وكلما فعل على وجه الذلة والاهانة. وفي الآخرة عذاب الأبد

sources.gloss: The sense of His words 'as for' is the detail of what was put summarily … Their punishment in this world is their abasement by killing, captivity, enslavement, ignominy and the jizya, and all that is done by way of humiliation and insult; and in the hereafter, everlasting punishment.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لأنه تفصيل ما أجمل في قوله: { ثم إلي مرجعكم فأحكم بينكم فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون }

sources.gloss: Because it is the detail of what was put summarily in His words: 'Then to Me will be your return, whereat I will judge between you concerning that about which you used to differ.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: اشارة إلى الاخبار عن عيسى، وزكريا، ويحيى، عن الحواريين، واليهود من بني إسرائيل

sources.gloss: A reference to the reports about Jesus, Zechariah and John, about the disciples, and about the Jews of the Children of Israel.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فقياس خلق عيسى من غير ذكر كقياس خلق آدم بل هو فيه أوجب, لأنه في آدم من غير أنثى, ولا ذكر

sources.gloss: The analogy of Jesus's creation without a male is like the analogy of Adam's creation; indeed it is stronger in his case, since Adam was from neither female nor male.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: واستدل أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن أمير المؤمنين (ع) كان أفضل الصحابة من وجهين

sources.gloss: Our companions have argued from this verse that the Commander of the Faithful was the most excellent of the companions, on two grounds.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لأنه رفع من الأرض حيا و قبض روحه بين السماء و الأرض، ثم رفع إلى السماء و رد عليه روحه

sources.gloss: For he was raised from the earth alive, and his soul was taken between the heaven and the earth, then he was raised to the heaven and his soul was returned to him.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إلى شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، و أني رسول الله، و أن عيسى عبد مخلوق، يأكل و يشرب و يحدث

sources.gloss: To testifying that there is no god but God, that I am God's Messenger, and that Jesus is a created servant who eats, drinks and relieves himself.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فأخرج رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) من الأنفس معه أبي، و من البنين أنا و أخي، و من النساء فاطمة أمي من الناس جميعا

sources.gloss: So the Messenger of God brought out, from the souls, my father with him; from the sons, myself and my brother; and from the women, Fatimah my mother, out of all the people.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: متوفي أجلك ومؤخرك إلى أجلك المسمى عاصماً اياك من قتلهم أو قابضك من الأرض من توفيت مالي أو مميتك عن الشهوات العائقة عن العروج إلى عالم الملكوت { وَرَافِعُكَ إليَّ } إلى محل كرامتي ومقر ملائكتي

sources.gloss: Completing your term and deferring you to your appointed time, protecting you from their killing; or seizing you from the earth; or making you die to the appetites that hinder the ascent to the world of the kingdom. 'And raising you up toward Myself': to the place of My honour and the abode of My angels.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: قال ٱبن عباس: هم أهل نجران: السيد والعاقب وٱبن الحارث رؤساؤهم … هذه الآية من أعلام نبوّة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه دعاهم إلى المباهلة فأبوا منها ورضوا بالجزية

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas said: they are the people of Najran, al-Sayyid, al-Aqib and Ibn al-Harith, their chiefs … This verse is among the marks of Muhammad's prophethood, for he called them to the mubahala and they refused it and accepted the jizya.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: فاقطع الكلام معهم وعاملهم بما يعامل به المعاند، وهو أن تدعوهم إلى الملاعنة

sources.gloss: So break off the discussion with them and deal with them as an obstinate man is dealt with, namely that you call them to mutual cursing.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: فَأَبْرَزَ النَّبِيُ‏ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ عَلِيّاً وَالْحَسَنَ وَالْحُسَيْنَ وَفَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلاَمُ وَقَرَنَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ بِنَفْسِهِ … إِنَّمَا عَنَى بِهَا عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ

sources.gloss: The Prophet brought forward Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and Fatimah, and joined their souls to his own … By it He meant Ali ibn Abi Talib.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: ان نفسي نفس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله والنساء فاطمة عليها السلام والابناء الحسن والحسين

sources.gloss: My soul is the soul of the Messenger of God, the women is Fatimah, and the sons are al-Hasan and al-Husayn.

essay.en:
The dispute over Jesus closes and an invitation opens. Al-Safi records the observation that the Prophet had set out what Jesus was, then called the delegation to the mutual imprecation, and when they drew back he returned to guiding them and took an easier and more binding road, calling them to what Jesus, the Gospel and the rest of the prophets and the books agree upon [21]. Sawa means just, even-handed between the two sides [2], and Tabatabai reads the summons as a call to take up that word together, spreading it and acting by what it requires, not merely saying it [1]. Its content is three: that God alone be worshipped, that nothing be made His partner, and that none of us take another as a lord. Tabrisi records the dispute over that last clause, whether it refuses Jesus as lord or the obedience given to rabbis, as in 9:31 [2]; Tusi makes the second sense the ground for holding the address is to the Jews of Madinah, over against the Christians of Najran, or, on the plain wording, both groups together [7].

A second question follows. Why argue over Abraham, when the Torah and the Gospel came down long after him? Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah report that Jewish rabbis and the Christians of Najran met before the Prophet, each side claiming him [3]. Qummi draws the next verse's contrast finely: they argued about what they had knowledge of, what stands in the Torah and the Gospel, and about what they had no knowledge of, what was in the scrolls of Abraham [15]. Verse 67 answers plainly, and Tusi holds Jew and Christian to be terms of blame, so that Moses was no Jew and Jesus no Christian, Judaism being a creed altered from the law of Moses [10].

Then the ground shifts from ancestry to following. The nearest to Abraham are those who followed him, this prophet and those who have faith, which Tabrisi takes as proof that walayah is established by religion and not by lineage [4]. The close is a warning: a group wished the believers astray, and the ruin of it returns on none but themselves [5]; two last questions ask why they deny signs they witness and mix truth with falsehood knowingly.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أن الكلمة هاهنا هي شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، و أن محمدا رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)، و أن عيسى عبد الله، و أنه مخلوق كآدم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani, narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad

text.en: The word here is the testimony that there is no god but God, that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, that Jesus is a servant of God, and that he is created like Adam.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما عبدوهم من دون الله ولكن حرموا لـهم حلالاً وأحلّوا لـهم حراماً فكان ذلك اتخاذهم أرباباً من دون الله

text.en: They did not worship them apart from God, but they forbade to them what was lawful and made lawful for them what was forbidden, and that was their taking them as lords apart from God.

note.en: Tusi gives two senses of hanif: upright in religion, since hanaf is uprightness in the language, or inclining toward the truth in religion [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: لا يهوديا يصلي إلى المغرب، و لا نصرانيا يصلي إلى المشرق { وَلَكِن كَانَ حَنِيفاً مُّسْلِماً } يقول: كان على دين محمد
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Not a Jew praying toward the west, nor a Christian praying toward the east. 'Rather, he was a Hanif, a Muslim': he was upon the religion of Muhammad.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: خالصاً مخلصاً ليس فيه شيء من عبادة الأوثان
narrations.chain: al-Kafi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: Pure and sincere, with nothing in it of the worship of idols.

note.en: Tusi glosses awla as the most entitled to support Abraham, whether by aid, as those with him in his time did, or by argument [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِالْأَنْبِيَاءِ أَعْلَمُهُمْ بِمَا جَاءُوا بِهِ … إِنَّ وَلِيَّ مُحَمَّد مَنْ أَطَاعَ اللهَ وإِنْ بَعُدَتْ لُحْمَتُهُ، وَإِنَّ عَدُوَّ مُحَمَّد مَنْ عَصَى اللهَ وَإِنْ قَرُبَتْ قَرَابَتُهُ

text.en: The nearest of people to the prophets are those who know best what they brought. Then he recited this verse and said: the friend of Muhammad is whoever obeys God, though his kinship be distant, and the enemy of Muhammad is whoever disobeys God, though his relation be near.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هُمُ الائِمَّةُ (عَلَيْهم السَّلام) وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَهُمْ
narrations.chain: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mualla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Muthanna, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, from Abu Jafar

text.en: They are the Imams and those who follow them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنتم والله من آل محمد فقلت من أنفسهم جعلت فداك؟ قال نعم والله من أنفسهم ثلاثاً … يا عمر إن الله يقول في كتابه { إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم للذين اتبعوه وهذا النبي والذين آمنوا والله ولي المؤمنين }
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Umar ibn Yazid

text.en: You are, by God, of the family of Muhammad. I said: of their very selves, may I be your ransom? He said: yes, by God, of their very selves, saying it three times. Then he said: Umar, God says in His book, 'Indeed the nearest of all people to Abraham are those who follow him.'

note.en: Fayd reports that the verse came down about the Jews when they called Hudhayfah, Ammar and Muadh to their religion [22].

Tabrisi glosses 'you testify' as knowing and seeing what proves the signs true and obliges acceptance of them, from the Torah and the Gospel, where the Prophet is named and his truthfulness announced [6].

Tusi reports from al-Hasan and other exegetes that the concealed truth is the Prophet's description and the tidings of him in their books, hidden by their scholars out of obstinacy [14]; Qummi reads it of the Torah [17].

perspectives.en: The traditions divide over who 'those who have faith' are. Al-Kafi carries al-Baqir's answer that they are the Imams and those who follow them [59], and Tabrisi reads the verse as proof that walayah rests on religion and not on lineage, citing Ali's word that the friend of Muhammad is whoever obeys God [4]. Tabari glosses the phrase as those who believed Muhammad and what he brought from God, and carries Ibn Masud's report that the Prophet said every prophet has protectors among the prophets, and his own is his father and his Lord's friend [27]. Ibn Kathir names the Muhajirun and Ansar among his companions and whoever followed them after [32].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالمعنى تعالوا نأخذ بهذه الكلمة متعاونين متعاضدين في نشرها والعمل بما توجبه

sources.gloss: The meaning is: come, let us take up this word, helping and supporting one another in spreading it and acting by what it requires.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: اختلف في معناه فقيل معناه ولا يتخذ بعضنا عيسى رّباً فإنه كان بعض الناس وقيل معناه أن لا نتخذ الأحبار أرباباً بأن نطيعهم طاعة الأرباب

sources.gloss: Its meaning was disputed. It was said to mean that none of us take Jesus as a lord, since he was one of the people; and it was said to mean that we not take the rabbis as lords by obeying them with the obedience due to lords.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة: إن أحبار اليهود ونصارى نجران اجتمعوا عند رسول الله فتنازعوا في إبراهيم

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: the Jewish rabbis and the Christians of Najran gathered before the Messenger of God and disputed over Abraham.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن الولاية تثبت بالدين لا بالنسب ويعضد ذلك قول أمير المؤمنين: إن أولى الناس بالأنبياء أعلمهم بما جاؤوا به

sources.gloss: In this verse is proof that walayah is established by religion and not by lineage, supported by the word of Amir al-Muminin: the nearest of people to the prophets are those who know best what they brought.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: معناه لا يرجع وبال إضلالـهم إلا على أنفسهم ولا يلحق ضرره إلا بهم

sources.gloss: Its meaning is that the ruin of their leading astray returns on none but themselves, and its harm reaches none but them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وأنتم تشهدون } أي تعلمون وتشاهدون ما يدل على صحتها ووجوب الإقرار بها من التوراة والإنجيل إذ فيهما ذكر النبي والإخبار بصدق نبوته

sources.gloss: 'While you testify': that is, you know and see what proves them true and obliges acknowledgement of them, from the Torah and the Gospel, since in them is the mention of the Prophet and the announcement of the truth of his prophethood.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ووجه هذا القول أنهم أطاعوا الاحبار طاعة الأرباب، فسلكوا بهم طريق الضلال … الثالث - ذكره أبو علي الجبائي أنها في الفريقين من أهل الكتاب على ظاهر الكلام

sources.gloss: The ground of this view is that they obeyed the rabbis with the obedience due to lords, so they led them along the road of misguidance ... The third view, given by Abu Ali al-Jubbai, is that it concerns both groups of the People of the Book, on the plain wording.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فأما اليهودية والنصرانية فصفتا ذم قد دل القرآن والاجماع على ذلك، لأن موسى لم يكن يهودياً، وعيسى لم يكن نصرانياً … وقيل في معنى الحنيف قولان: أحدهما - المستقيم الدين، لأن الحنف هو الاستقامة في اللغة

sources.gloss: As for Judaism and Christianity, they are two descriptions of blame, as the Quran and consensus show, since Moses was not a Jew and Jesus was not a Christian ... And on the meaning of hanif two things are said: one, upright in religion, since hanaf is uprightness in the language.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أي أحقهم بنصرته بالمعونة أو الحجة، لأن الذين اتبعوه في زمانه تولوه بالنصرة على عدوه

sources.gloss: That is, the most entitled to support him, whether by aid or by argument, for those who followed him in his time took up his support against his enemy.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والحق الذي كتموه - في قول الحسن، وغيره من المفسرين -: هو ما وجدوه من صفة النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) والبشارة به في كتبهم على وجه العناد من علمائهم

sources.gloss: The truth they concealed, in the view of al-Hasan and other exegetes, is what they found of the description of the Prophet and the tidings of him in their books, concealed out of obstinacy by their scholars.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: حاججتم فيما لكم به علم } يعني بما في التوراة والإِنجيل { فلم تحاجون فيما ليس لكم به علم } يعني بما في صحف إبراهيم

sources.gloss: 'You argue about that of which you have knowledge': that is, about what is in the Torah and the Gospel. 'Why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge': that is, about what is in the scrolls of Abraham.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أنتم والله من آل محمد فقلت من أنفسهم جعلت فداك؟ قال نعم والله من أنفسهم ثلاثاً

sources.gloss: You are, by God, of the family of Muhammad. I said: of their very selves, may I be your ransom? He said: yes, by God, of their very selves, three times.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أي: تعلمون ما في التوراة من صفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وتكتمونه

sources.gloss: That is, you know what is in the Torah of the description of the Messenger of God and you conceal it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أن الكلمة هاهنا هي شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، و أن محمدا رسول الله

sources.gloss: The word here is the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لا يهوديا يصلي إلى المغرب، و لا نصرانيا يصلي إلى المشرق

sources.gloss: Not a Jew praying toward the west, nor a Christian praying toward the east.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: قيل انظر إلى ما راعى في هذه القصة من المبالغة في الارشاد وحسن التدرج في الحجاج بيّن أولاً احوال عيسى … فلما رأى عنادهم ولجاجهم دعاهم إلى المباهلة بنوع من الاعجاز ثم لما اعرضوا عنها وانقادوا بعض الانقياد عاد عليهم بالارشاد وسلك طريقاً أسهل وألزم بأن دعاهم إلى ما وافق عليه عيسى والانجيل وسائر الأنبياء والكتب

sources.gloss: It is said: look at the care taken in this story, the thoroughness in guidance and the fine gradation in argument. He first set out the states of Jesus ... then when he saw their obstinacy and wrangling he called them to the mutual imprecation by a kind of miracle; then when they turned from it and yielded somewhat, he returned to guiding them and took an easier and more binding road, calling them to what Jesus, the Gospel, and the rest of the prophets and books agreed upon.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: قيل نزلت في اليهود لما دعوا حذيفة وعماراً ومعاذاً إلى اليهودية … خالصاً مخلصاً ليس فيه شيء من عبادة الأوثان

sources.gloss: It is said that it came down about the Jews when they called Hudhayfah, Ammar and Muadh to Judaism ... Pure and sincere, with nothing in it of the worship of idols.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: يعنـي والذين صدّقوا مـحمداً، وبـما جاءهم به من عند الله … إنَّ لِكُلّ نَبِـيّ وُلاةً مِنَ النَّبِـيِّـينَ، وَإنَّ وَلِـيِّـي مِنْهُمْ أبـي وَخَـلِـيـلُ رَبّـي

sources.gloss: That is, those who believed Muhammad and what he brought them from God ... Every prophet has protectors among the prophets, and my protector among them is my father and the friend of my Lord.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: والذين آمنوا من أصحابه المهاجرين والأنصار ومن تبعهم بعدهم

sources.gloss: And those who believed, from among his companions, the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and whoever followed them after them.

sources.author: al-sharif al-radi

excerpt.text: إِنَّ وَلِيَّ مُحَمَّد مَنْ أَطَاعَ اللهَ وإِنْ بَعُدَتْ لُحْمَتُهُ، وَإِنَّ عَدُوَّ مُحَمَّد مَنْ عَصَى اللهَ وَإِنْ قَرُبَتْ قَرَابَتُهُ

sources.gloss: The friend of Muhammad is whoever obeys God, though his kinship be distant, and the enemy of Muhammad is whoever disobeys God, though his relation be near.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: هُمُ الائِمَّةُ (عَلَيْهم السَّلام) وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَهُمْ

sources.gloss: They are the Imams and those who follow them.

title.en: Believe at dawn, deny at dusk

essay.en:
A scheme, a slander, a disavowal. Tabatabai marks these verses as the start of a second stage in the surah's address, turning to the People of the Book at large and then to the Christians in particular [1].

It opens with a plan spoken among themselves: believe in the morning, disbelieve at evening, so that they may turn back. Tusi reports three views and holds the first, an outward profession at daybreak and a public retraction at dusk, to be the view of most scholars [8]; Qummi carries al-Baqir's account, which ties the whole scheme to the change of the qiblah [17]. The next line, do not believe anyone except him who follows your religion, al-Hasan assigns to the Jews of Khaybar speaking to the Jews of Madinah [9]. What follows is disputed even in its reading, the reciter Ibn Kathir lengthening the alif so that it asks a question, the rest reading it flat [3]; and Fayd Kashani places the clause among the ambiguous verses on which nothing has reached us from the Ahl al-Bayt [30]. The reply cuts across it: guidance is God's guidance, grace is in God's hand.

Then a ledger of trust. One man returns a quintal, another withholds a dinar. Tabrisi names Abdullah ibn Salam and Finhas ibn Azura from Ibn Abbas [4], and Tusi gives their excuse in two forms: that Arab wealth was lawful as the wealth of idolaters, or that these men had left the religion on which the dealing was made [11]. The threat that follows is fixed to occasions: rabbis who hid what the Torah said of Muhammad so as not to lose their leadership [5]. Verse 78 returns to the forgers, which Majma al-Bayan reports came down about rabbis who wrote with their own hands what is not in God's book and ascribed it to it [6], while Tusi says 'of them' points back to the People of the Book of verse 75, and reports from Mujahid, Qatada, Ibn Jurayj and al-Rabi that twisting the tongue means altering and substituting [14].

The close clears the prophets. Tabatabai reads it as a second chapter of the argument acquitting the Messiah [2]; Tabrisi gives the occasion, Abu Rafi and the chief of Najran asking whether he wanted to be worshipped [7]; and rabbaniyyin, Tusi reports, means scholars and jurists, wise and godfearing, teachers of the people [15]. The last verse, he adds, came to belie the claim that the Messiah ordered his own worship [16].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله لما قدم المدينة وهو يصلي نحو بيت المقدس أعجب اليهود من ذلك فلما صرفه الله عن بيت المقدس إلى بيت الحرام وجدت وكان صرف القبلة صلاة الظهر فقالوا صلى محمد الغداة واستقبل قبلتنا فآمنوا بالذي أنزل على محمد وجه النهار واكفروا آخره
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: When the Messenger of God came to Madinah he prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis, and the Jews were pleased. When God turned him to the Sacred House, at the noon prayer, they said: Muhammad prayed the dawn facing our qiblah, so believe in what was sent down to Muhammad at the day's beginning and disbelieve at its end.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: يا كميل: { ٱلْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ } ، { وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ } يا كميل: علام يحسدوننا، و الله أنشأنا من قبل أن يعرفونا، أ فتراهم بحسدهم إيانا عن ربنا يزيلوننا؟!
narrations.chain: Bisharat al-Mustafa, from Said ibn Zayd ibn Artah, from Kumayl ibn Ziyad, from Amir al-Muminin Ali

text.en: O Kumayl: 'all grace is in Allah's hand; He grants it to whomever He wishes', 'and Allah is dispenser of a great grace'. O Kumayl, why do they envy us? By God, He brought us into being before they knew us. Do you think their envy can remove us from our Lord?

note.en: Tusi finds here a proof that prophethood is not deserved by deeds: were it a recompense, it could not be said that He singles out with it whomever He wishes [10].

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: كذب اعداء الله ما من شيء كان في الجاهلية الا وهو تحت قدمي الا الأمانة فانها مؤدات إلى البر والفاجر
narrations.chain: in Majma al-Bayan, from the Prophet, when he recited this verse

text.en: The enemies of God have lied. There is nothing of the age of ignorance but it is under my feet, except the trust, for it is to be rendered to the righteous and the wicked.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: فإن اليهود قالوا: يحل لنا أن نأخذ مال الأُميين والأُمييون الذين ليس معهم كتاب

text.en: The Jews said: it is lawful for us to take the wealth of the unlettered. The unlettered are those who have no scripture with them.

note.en: Tusi cites al-Zajjaj: bala is a complete stop here. When they said there is no way against us over the unlettered, the answer came, yes, there is a way against them [12].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أنزل في العهد … و الخلاق: النصيب، فمن لم يكن له نصيب في الآخرة فبأي شيء يدخل الجنة؟!
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from Abd al-Razzaq ibn Mihran, from al-Husayn ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: This was sent down concerning the covenant. Al-khalaq is the share; and whoever has no share in the Hereafter, by what thing will he enter the Garden?

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: وأما قوله: (لا ينظر إليهم يوم القيمة) يخبر أنه لا يصيبهم بخير، وقد تقول العرب: والله ما ينظر إلينا فلان، وإنما يعنون بذلك أنه لا يصيبنا منه بخير، فذلك النظر ههنا من الله تعالى إلى خلقه، فنظره إليهم رحمة منه لهم
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, from Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, from Ahmad ibn Yaqub ibn Matar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Talhah ibn Yazid, from Ubaydullah ibn Ubayd, from Abu Mamar al-Sadani

text.en: As for His word, nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection: He is telling that He will not touch them with any good. The Arabs say, by God, so and so does not look at us, meaning only that no good reaches us from him. His looking at them is a mercy from Him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وَالَْيمِينُ الْغَمُوسُ، لأنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمانِهِمْ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً أُولئِكَ لا خَلاقَ لَهُمْ فِي الآْخِرَةِ)
narrations.chain: Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida, from his father al-Rida, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Jafar

text.en: And the false oath, because God says: 'There shall be no share in the Hereafter for those who sell Allah's covenant and their oaths for a paltry gain.'

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: كان اليهود يقولون شيئا ليس في التوراة، و يقولون هو في التوراة فكذبهم الله

text.en: The Jews used to say a thing that is not in the Torah and say that it is in the Torah, so God belied them.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: لا تَرْفَعُونِي فَوْقَ حَقِّي فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى اتَّخَذَنِي عَبْداً قَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَنِي نَبِيّاً
narrations.chain: al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Jafar, from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib

text.en: Do not raise me above my right, for God, blessed and exalted, took me as a servant before He took me as a prophet.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: يَهْلِكُ فِيَّ اثْنَانِ وَلا ذَنْبَ لِي مُحِبٌّ مُفْرِطٌ وَمُبْغِضٌ مُفْرِطٌ وَإِنَّا لَنَبْرَأُ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ مِمَّنْ يَغْلُو فِينَا فَيَرْفَعُنَا فَوْقَ حَدِّنَا كَبَرَاءَةِ عِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ مِنَ النَّصَارَى
narrations.chain: al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Jafar, from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib

text.en: Two are destroyed on my account and I have no sin: a lover who goes to excess and a hater who goes to excess. We declare ourselves clear before God of whoever exceeds bounds about us and raises us above our limit, as Jesus son of Mary was clear of the Christians.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: إن عيسى لم يقل للناس: إني خلقتكم فكونوا عبادا لي من دون الله، و لكن قال لهم: كونوا ربانيين، أي علماء

text.en: Jesus did not say to the people, I created you, so be servants to me apart from God. Rather he said to them, be godly people, that is, scholars.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: كان قوم يعبدون الملائكة، و قوم من النصارى زعموا أن عيسى (عليه السلام) رب، و اليهود قالوا: عزير ابن الله

text.en: A people used to worship the angels, and a group of the Christians claimed that Jesus is a lord, and the Jews said Uzayr is the son of God.

perspectives.en: Verses 79 and 80 are applied differently. Fayd Kashani carries from Uyun the Prophet's word, do not raise me above my right, for God took me as a servant before He took me as a prophet, and follows it with Ali's disavowal of those who exalt his household beyond their limit, as Jesus was clear of the Christians [31]. Ibn Kathir turns the verse outward, to the ignorant among the rabbis, monks and misguiding shaykhs, who fall under this censure while the messengers and the scholars who act on their knowledge do not [45].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان شروع في المرحلة الثانية من البيان المتعرض لحال أهل الكتاب عامة والنصارى خاصة وما يلحق بذلك

sources.gloss: An exposition beginning the second stage of the discourse, which treats the state of the People of the Book generally and the Christians in particular, and what attaches to that.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وقوع الآيات عقيب الآيات المرتبطة بأمر عيسى عليه السلام يفيد أنها بمنزلة الفصل الثاني من الاحتجاج على براءة ساحة المسيح مما يعتقده في حقه أهل الكتاب من النصارى

sources.gloss: That these verses fall after the verses bound up with the affair of Jesus shows that they stand as the second chapter of the argument for the Messiah's innocence of what the Christians among the People of the Book believe of him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قرأ ابن كثير أن يؤتى أحد ممدوداً والباقون أن يؤتى بغير مد واستفهام

sources.gloss: Ibn Kathir read 'that anyone may be given' with a lengthened alif, and the rest read it without lengthening and without a question.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: عن ابن عباس قال يعني بقولـه من أن تأمنه بقنطار يؤده إليك عبد الله بن سلام … ويعني بقولـه من أن تأمنه بدينار لا يؤدّه إليك فَنْحاص بن عزوراء

sources.gloss: From Ibn Abbas: by 'he who if you entrust him with a quintal will repay it to you' is meant Abdullah ibn Salam ... and by 'he who if you entrust him with a dinar will not repay it to you' is meant Finhas ibn Azura.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في جماعة من أحبار اليهود أبي رافع وكنانة بن أبي الحقيق وحيي بن الأخطب وكعب بن الأشرف كتموا ما في التوراة من أمر محمد وكتبوا بأيديهم غيره وحلفوا أنه من عند الله لئلا تفوتهم الرياسة

sources.gloss: It came down about a group of the Jewish rabbis, Abu Rafi, Kinanah ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Huyayy ibn al-Akhtab and Kab ibn al-Ashraf, who concealed what was in the Torah about Muhammad, wrote something else with their own hands and swore it was from God, so as not to lose their leadership.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل نزلت في جماعة من أحبار اليهود كتبوا بأيديهم ما ليس في كتاب الله من نعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وغيره وأضافوه إلى كتاب الله

sources.gloss: It is said that it came down about a group of the Jewish rabbis who wrote with their own hands what is not in God's book, of the description of the Prophet and other matters, and attached it to God's book.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل إن أبا رافع الفُرَضي من اليهود ورئيس وفد نجران قالا يا محمد أتريد أن نعبدك ونتخذك إلـهاً فقال: " معاذ الله أن أعبد غير الله أو آمر بعبادة غير الله ما بذلك بعثني ولا بذلك أمرني

sources.gloss: It is said that Abu Rafi al-Furadi of the Jews and the chief of the delegation of Najran said: Muhammad, do you want us to worship you and take you as a god? He said: God forbid that I should worship other than God, or command the worship of other than God. Not for that did He send me, nor with that did He command me.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أولها - أظهروا الايمان لهم في أول النهار وارجعوا عنه في آخره، فانه أحرى أن ينقلبوا عن دينهم … والوجه الأول قول أكثر أهل العلم

sources.gloss: The first: show them faith at the beginning of the day and turn back from it at its end, for that is likelier to make them turn from their religion ... The first view is the saying of most of the people of knowledge.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الحسن: القائلين { لا تؤمنوا إلا لمن تبع دينكم } هم يهود خيبر ليهود المدينة

sources.gloss: Al-Hasan said: those who said 'do not believe anyone except him who follows your religion' were the Jews of Khaybar, to the Jews of Madinah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على أن النبوة ليست مستحقة بالافعال، لأنها لو كانت جزاء، لما جاز أن يقول يختص بها من يشاء

sources.gloss: In the verse is proof that prophethood is not deserved by deeds, for had it been a recompense it would not have been right for Him to say that He singles out with it whomever He wishes.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال قتادة والسدي: قالت اليهود ليس علينا فيما أصبنا من أموال العرب سبيل، لأنهم مشركون. و [الثاني] قال الحسن وابن جريج: لأنهم تحولوا عن دينهم الذي عاملناهم عليه وادعوا أنهم وجدوا ذلك في كتابهم

sources.gloss: Qatadah and al-Suddi said: the Jews said there is no way against us over what we take of the Arabs' wealth, because they are idolaters. The second: al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj said, because they turned away from the religion on which we dealt with them, and they claimed they found that in their book.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال الزجاج: بلى ها هنا وقف تام لأنهم لما قالوا { ليس علينا في الأميين سبيل } قيل { بلى } أي بلى عليهم سبيل

sources.gloss: Al-Zajjaj said: bala here is a complete stop, for when they said 'we have no obligation to the non-Jews' it was said, yes, there is a way against them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الكناية بالهاء والميم راجعة على أهل الكتاب في قوله: { من أهل الكتاب من إن تأمنه بقنطار } في قول جميع المفسرين … قال مجاهد، وقتادة، وابن جريج، والربيع: معناه يحرفونه بالتغيير والتبديل

sources.gloss: The pronoun in 'of them' goes back to the People of the Book in His word 'among the People of the Book is he who if you entrust him with a quintal', by the saying of all the exegetes ... Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj and al-Rabi said: its meaning is that they distort it by alteration and substitution.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعناه في قول الحسن: علماء فقهاء. وقالو سعيد بن جبير: حكماء أتقياء. وقال ابن أبي رزين: حكماء علماء. وقال الزجاج: معناه معلمي الناس

sources.gloss: Its meaning, in al-Hasan's saying, is scholars and jurists. Said ibn Jubayr said: wise and godfearing. Ibn Abi Razin said: wise and learned. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is teachers of the people.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والآية خرجت مخرج التكذيب لهم في دعواهم أن المسيح أمرهم بعبادته

sources.gloss: The verse came out in the manner of belying them in their claim that the Messiah commanded them to worship him.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله لما قدم المدينة وهو يصلي نحو بيت المقدس أعجب اليهود من ذلك فلما صرفه الله عن بيت المقدس إلى بيت الحرام وجدت وكان صرف القبلة صلاة الظهر فقالوا صلى محمد الغداة واستقبل قبلتنا فآمنوا بالذي أنزل على محمد وجه النهار واكفروا آخره

sources.gloss: That the Messenger of God, when he came to Madinah, was praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis, and the Jews were pleased at that; and when God turned him from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Sacred House, the turning of the qiblah being at the noon prayer, they said: Muhammad prayed the dawn facing our qiblah, so believe in what was sent down to Muhammad at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فإن اليهود قالوا: يحل لنا أن نأخذ مال الأُميين والأُمييون الذين ليس معهم كتاب

sources.gloss: For the Jews said: it is lawful for us to take the wealth of the unlettered; and the unlettered are those who have no scripture with them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يا كميل: { ٱلْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ } ، { وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ } يا كميل: علام يحسدوننا، و الله أنشأنا من قبل أن يعرفونا، أ فتراهم بحسدهم إيانا عن ربنا يزيلوننا؟!

sources.gloss: O Kumayl: 'all grace is in Allah's hand; He grants it to whomever He wishes', 'and Allah is dispenser of a great grace'. O Kumayl, for what do they envy us? By God, He brought us into being before they knew us. Do you think that by their envy of us they can remove us from our Lord?

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أنزل في العهد … و الخلاق: النصيب، فمن لم يكن له نصيب في الآخرة فبأي شيء يدخل الجنة؟!

sources.gloss: It was sent down concerning the covenant ... and al-khalaq is the share; so whoever has no share in the Hereafter, by what thing will he enter the Garden?

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: كان اليهود يقولون شيئا ليس في التوراة، و يقولون هو في التوراة فكذبهم الله … إن عيسى لم يقل للناس: إني خلقتكم فكونوا عبادا لي من دون الله، و لكن قال لهم: كونوا ربانيين، أي علماء

sources.gloss: The Jews used to say a thing that is not in the Torah and say it is in the Torah, so God belied them ... Jesus did not say to the people, I created you, so be servants to me apart from God; rather he said to them, be godly people, that is, scholars.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: كان قوم يعبدون الملائكة، و قوم من النصارى زعموا أن عيسى (عليه السلام) رب، و اليهود قالوا: عزير ابن الله

sources.gloss: A people used to worship the angels, and a group of the Christians claimed that Jesus is a lord, and the Jews said Uzayr is the son of God.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وفي الآية وجوه أُخر وهي من المتشابهات التي لم يصل إلينا عن أهل البيت شيء

sources.gloss: In the verse are other faces, and it is among the ambiguous passages about which nothing has reached us from the Ahl al-Bayt.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: لا ترفعوني فوق حقي فان الله تعالى اتخذني عبداً قبل أن يتخذني نبياً … يهلك فيّ اثنان ولا ذنب لي محب مفرط ومبغض مفرط وانا لبراء إلى الله تعالى ممن يغلو فينا فيرفعنا فوق حدّنا كبراءة عيسى بن مريم من النصارى

sources.gloss: Do not raise me above my right, for God took me as a servant before He took me as a prophet ... Two are destroyed on my account and I have no sin: a lover who goes to excess and a hater who goes to excess; and I am clear before God of whoever exceeds bounds about us and raises us above our limit, as Jesus son of Mary was clear of the Christians.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: فالجهلة من الأحبار والرهبان ومشايخ الضلال يدخلون في هذا الذم والتوبيخ

sources.gloss: So the ignorant among the rabbis, the monks and the shaykhs of misguidance fall under this censure and rebuke.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: وَالَْيمِينُ الْغَمُوسُ، لأنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمانِهِمْ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً أُولئِكَ لا خَلاقَ لَهُمْ فِي الآْخِرَةِ)

sources.gloss: And the false oath, because God, mighty and majestic, says: 'Indeed those who sell Allah's covenant and their oaths for a paltry gain, there shall be no share for them in the Hereafter.'

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: وأما قوله: (لا ينظر إليهم يوم القيمة) يخبر أنه لا يصيبهم بخير، وقد تقول العرب: والله ما ينظر إلينا فلان، وإنما يعنون بذلك أنه لا يصيبنا منه بخير، فذلك النظر ههنا من الله تعالى إلى خلقه، فنظره إليهم رحمة منه لهم

sources.gloss: As for His word 'nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection': He tells that He will not touch them with any good. The Arabs say, by God, so and so does not look at us, meaning only that no good reaches us from him. That looking here is God's looking at His creation, and His looking at them is a mercy from Him.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: لا تَرْفَعُونِي فَوْقَ حَقِّي فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى اتَّخَذَنِي عَبْداً قَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَنِي نَبِيّاً … يَهْلِكُ فِيَّ اثْنَانِ وَلا ذَنْبَ لِي مُحِبٌّ مُفْرِطٌ وَمُبْغِضٌ مُفْرِطٌ وَإِنَّا لَنَبْرَأُ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ مِمَّنْ يَغْلُو فِينَا فَيَرْفَعُنَا فَوْقَ حَدِّنَا كَبَرَاءَةِ عِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ

sources.gloss: Do not raise me above my right, for God, blessed and exalted, took me as a servant before He took me as a prophet ... Two are destroyed on my account and I have no sin: a lover who goes to excess and a hater who goes to excess. We declare ourselves clear before God of whoever exceeds bounds about us and raises us above our limit, as Jesus son of Mary was clear of the Christians.

essay.en:
The passage answers a claim with a covenant. Tabatabai reads it as continuous with what precedes: God bound every prophet to believe in and help any prophet who comes to him, earlier or later, each confirming the one before him and announcing the one after, as Jesus confirmed Moses and announced Muhammad [1]. Al-Tabrisi reports from Amir al-Muminin, Ibn Abbas and Qatada that the prophets were to tell their communities of Muhammad's coming and command them to affirm him, and from Tawus that the earlier were bound to believe in what the later would bring [3]. Al-Tusi asks how a prophet helps a messenger he will not live to meet: by confirming him before his own people [8]. Of those who turn away the verse says ‘transgressors’, not ‘disbelievers’; al-Tusi explains that they are the rebellious within their disbelief [9].

Verse 83 asks whether they seek a religion other than God's. Al-Tabrisi records the occasion: factions of the People of the Book brought their quarrel over Abraham's religion to the Prophet, who declared both free of it, and they refused his judgment [4]. The Prophet is then made to answer for himself and his community, believing in all that was sent down without distinction; al-Tusi records as one of two readings that this refuses those who accept some prophets and reject others [11]. Then the rule: no religion but Islam is accepted. Al-Tusi reports from Ikrima that when Jews claimed the name, the verse of hajj came down, they held back from it, and their claim was undone [12].

The last six verses turn to faith abandoned after proof. Al-Tabrisi reports that verses 86 to 89 came down about Harith ibn Suwayd of the Ansar, who killed a man treacherously, fled to Mecca an apostate, then asked whether repentance was open to him [5]. Tabatabai reads ‘How shall Allah guide’ as denial rather than question: guidance is withheld while that description holds in them, which does not exclude His guiding them should they return and repent [2]. The repentance refused in verse 90, al-Tabrisi says, was never sincere, and the closing words name them astray to show it [6]. The passage ends with the man who dies denying, whom al-Tabrisi pictures, on Qatada's report, asked at the Resurrection whether he would ransom himself with a world of gold, and told he was once asked something easier [7].

note.en: ‘My covenant’ renders isri, glossed as ‘My pledge’; the narration places the exchange in the world of particles, and it is the angels whom God calls to witness [23].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وإذا أخذ الله ميثاق امم النبيين كل امة بتصديق نبيها والعمل بما جاءهم به فما وفوا به وتركوا كثيراً من شرائعهم وحرّفوا كثيراً منها

text.en: And when God took the compact of the communities of the prophets, each community to affirm its prophet and to act by what he brought them. They did not keep it: they abandoned much of their laws and distorted much of them.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ان الله تعالى أخذ الميثاق على الأنبياء قبل نبيّنا ان يخبروا اممهم بمبعثه ونعته ويبشّروهم به ويأمروهم بتصديقه

text.en: God took the compact upon the prophets before our Prophet that they should tell their communities of his mission and his description, give them glad tidings of him, and command them to affirm him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما بعث الله نبيا من لدن آدم (عليه السلام) فهلم جرا إلا و يرجع إلى الدنيا و ينصر أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام)، و هو قوله: { لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ } يعني رسول الله { وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُ } يعني أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام)
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God has sent no prophet, from Adam onward, but that he will return to the world and help Amir al-Muminin. That is His word, ‘you shall believe in him’, meaning the Messenger of God, ‘and help him’, meaning Amir al-Muminin.

note.en: Fayd Kashani relays al-Ayyashi's report from Imam al-Sadiq that the verse was revealed about the Qaim, and a report that when he rises no land will be left without the testimony proclaimed in it [26].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كرهاً أي فَرَقاً من السيف

text.en: ‘Unwillingly’, that is, out of fear of the sword.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فقال أصحاب اليمين: بلى يا ربنا، نحن بريتك و خلقك مقرين طائعين. و قال أصحاب الشمال: بلى يا ربنا نحن بريتك و خلقك كارهين … و ذلك قول الله: { وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ } - قال-: توحيدهم لله
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The companions of the right said: Yes, our Lord, we are Your creatures, acknowledging, willing. The companions of the left said: Yes, our Lord, we are Your creatures, unwilling. That is God's word, ‘to Him submits whoever there is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly’. He said: their affirming God's oneness.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: { وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ } أ كان ذلك بعد؟
narrations.chain: from Abaya al-Asadi, who heard Amir al-Muminin say it

text.en: ‘To Him submits whoever there is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be brought back.’ Has that happened yet?

note.en: Al-Qummi marks this verse muhkam, definitive [21].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: فاتقوا الله في سرائركم وعلانيتكم ولا تموتن الا وأنتم مسلمون ومن يبتغ غير الاسلام ديناً فلن يقبل منه وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Sad ibn Abd Allah, from Abu al-Jawza, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Hurmuz al-Haddad, from Sad ibn Zarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata

text.en: So fear God in your private and your public affairs, and do not die except as Muslims; for whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it shall never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.

note.en: Al-Tusi records al-Hasan's view that the verse came down about People of the Book who believed in the Prophet from his description and proofs in their books, then denied him once God sent him [13].
Al-Tusi asks why amending is stipulated with repentance, and answers that it removes the illusion that once faith and repentance from disbelief are had, no ugly deed can harm a person [16].
Al-Tusi relays al-Zajjaj's reading of the ransom: had such a man given it in this world while holding to his disbelief, it would not have been accepted from him [18].

perspectives.en: Both traditions read the compact of verse 81 as binding the earlier prophets to Muhammad. Al-Tabrisi reports it from Amir al-Muminin, Ibn Abbas and Qatada [3]; Ibn Kathir reports the same from Ali and Ibn Abbas, and holds that the view of Tawus, al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatada, that the prophets confirm one another, does not contradict it but is required by it [36]. They part over the two verbs. The narrations al-Bahrani collects refer ‘you shall believe in him’ to the Messenger of God and ‘you shall help him’ to Amir al-Muminin [23], where Ibn Kathir refers both to the messenger who comes later [36].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وقد أخذ الله الميثاق من النبيين أن يؤمنوا بكل نبي يأتيهم ممن تقدمهم أو تأخر عنهم وينصروه وذلك بتصديق كل منهم لمن تقدم عليه من الأنبياء وتبشيره بمن تأخر عنه

sources.gloss: God took the compact from the prophets that they believe in and help every prophet who comes to them, whether before them or after them, and that is by each one affirming the prophets before him and announcing the one after him.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أي لا يهديهم مع وجود هذا الوصف فيهم وذلك لا ينافي هدايته لهم على تقدير رجوعهم وتوبتهم منه

sources.gloss: That is, He does not guide them while this description is in them; and that does not conflict with His guiding them should they turn back and repent of it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وروي عن أمير المؤمنين ع وابن عباس وقتادة أن الله أخذ الميثاق على الأنبياء قبل نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يخبروا أممهم بمبعثه ونفعته ويبشروهم به ويأمروهم بتصديقه وقال طاووس: أخذ الله الميثاق على الأنبياء ع على الأول والآخر فأخذ الله ميثاق الأول لتأمنن بما جاء به الآخر

sources.gloss: It is narrated from Amir al-Muminin, Ibn Abbas and Qatada that God took the compact upon the prophets before our Prophet that they should tell their communities of his mission and his description, give them glad tidings of him and command them to affirm him. Tawus said: God took the compact upon the prophets, the first and the last, so He took the compact of the first that ‘you shall believe in what the last brings’.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: اختصم أهل الكتاب إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما اختلفوا بينهم من دين إبراهيم كل فرقة زعمت أنهم أولى بدينه فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

sources.gloss: The People of the Book brought their dispute to the Messenger of God over what they differed about in the religion of Abraham, each faction claiming it was closer to his religion, and the Prophet said [that both parties are free of the religion of Abraham].

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل نزلت الآيات في رجل من الأنصار يقال لـه حارث بن سويد بن الصامت وكان قتل المجذر بن زياد البلوي غدراً وهرب وارتد عن الإسلام ولحق بمكة ثم ندم فأرسل إلى قومه أن يسألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هل لي من توبة فسألوا فنزلت الآية إلى قولـه { إلا الذين تابوا }

sources.gloss: It is said the verses came down about a man of the Ansar called Harith ibn Suwayd ibn al-Samit, who had treacherously killed Mujadhdhar ibn Ziyad al-Balawi, then fled and apostatized from Islam and joined Mecca; then he regretted it and sent to his people to ask the Messenger of God whether there was any repentance for him. So they asked, and the verse came down, down to His words ‘except such as repent’.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لأنها لم تقع على وجه الإخلاص ويدل عليه قولـه { وأولئك هم الضالون } ولو حقّقوا في التوبة لكانوا مهتدين

sources.gloss: Because it did not occur in the way of sincerity, as His words ‘and it is they who are the astray’ indicate; had they been true in their repentance they would have been guided.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال قتادة: يجاء بالكافر يوم القيامة فيقال لـه أرأيت لو كان لك ملء الأرض ذهباً لكنت تفتدي به فيقول: نعم فيقال لـه: لقد سئلت أيسر من ذلك فلم تفعل

sources.gloss: Qatada said: the denier is brought on the Day of Resurrection and it is said to him, ‘Do you see, had you a world of gold, would you ransom yourself with it?’ He says, ‘Yes.’ It is said to him, ‘You were asked something easier than that, and you did not do it.’

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعنى أخذ الميثاق من النبيين بنصرة من لم يلقوه ولم يدركوا زمانه هو أنهم ينصرونه بتصديقه عند قومهم، ويأمرونهم بالاقرار به

sources.gloss: The meaning of taking the compact from the prophets to help one they did not meet and whose time they did not reach is that they help him by affirming him before their people and commanding them to acknowledge him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: التولي عن الايمان بالنبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) كفر - بلا خلاف - وإنما قال { فأولئك هم الفاسقون } ولم يقل الكافرون، لأن تقدير الكلام فأولئك هم الفاسقون في كفرهم أي المتمردون فيه بخروجهم إلى الأفحش منه

sources.gloss: Turning away from faith in the Prophet is disbelief, without dispute. He said ‘it is they who are the transgressors’ and did not say ‘the disbelievers’, because the sense is: they are the transgressors within their disbelief, that is, the rebellious in it, going out to what is uglier in it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قيل في تأويل هذه الآية قولان: أحدهما - أن معناها الانكار على الكفار ما ذهبوا إليه من الايمان ببعض النبيين دون بعض، فأمر الله تعالى النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم)، والمؤمنين أن يقولوا: إنا نؤمن بجميع النبيين، ولا نفرق بين أحد منهم

sources.gloss: Two readings have been given for the interpretation of this verse. The first of them: its meaning is a refusal of the deniers for what they held, believing in some of the prophets and not others; so God commanded the Prophet and the believers to say: we believe in all the prophets, and we make no distinction between any of them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال عكرمة: إن قوماً من اليهود قالوا: نحن المسلمون، فأنزل الله تعالى { ولله على الناس حج البيت } فأمرهم بالخروج إلى الحج الذي هو من فرض الاسلام، فقعدوا عنه وبان انسلاخهم من الاسلام، لمخالفتهم له

sources.gloss: Ikrima said: a people of the Jews said, ‘We are the Muslims.’ So God sent down ‘it is the duty of mankind toward Allah to make pilgrimage to the House’, commanding them to go out to the hajj, which is an obligation of Islam; they held back from it, and their stripping themselves of Islam became plain by their opposing it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الحسن: نزلت هذه الآية في أهل الكتاب الذين كانوا يؤمنون بالنبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قبل مبعثه بما يجدونه في كتبهم من صفاته ودلائله، فلما بعثه الله جحدوا ذلك، وانكروه

sources.gloss: Al-Hasan said: this verse came down about the People of the Book who used to believe in the Prophet before his mission, by what they found in their books of his description and his proofs; then, when God sent him, they denied that and rejected it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قيل الوجه في ذلك إزالة الابهام لئلا يعتقد، أنه إذا حصل الايمان، والتوبة من الكفر لا يضر معه شيء من أفعال القبائح

sources.gloss: The reason for it is the removal of ambiguity, so that it not be believed that once faith and repentance from disbelief are attained, nothing of ugly deeds harms a person along with them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والثاني - ما حكاه الزجاج أنه لو افتدى به في دار الدنيا مع الاقامة على الكفر لم يقبل منه

sources.gloss: The second is what al-Zajjaj related: that had he ransomed himself with it in this world while persisting in disbelief, it would not have been accepted from him.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وقوله: { ومن يبتغ غير الإِسلام دينا فلن يقبل منه } فإنه محكم

sources.gloss: And His words, ‘Should anyone follow a religion other than Islam, it shall never be accepted from him’: it is muhkam.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ثم قال لهم في الذر: { أَأَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلَىٰ ذٰلِكُمْ إِصْرِي } أي عهدي: { قَالُوۤاْ أَقْرَرْنَا قَالَ } الله للملائكة: { فَٱشْهَدُواْ وَأَنَاْ مَعَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلشَّاهِدِينَ }

sources.gloss: Then He said to them in the world of particles: ‘Do you pledge and accept My covenant on this condition?’, that is, My pledge. ‘They said, We pledge. He said’, God to the angels, ‘Then be witnesses, and I, too, am among the witnesses along with you.’

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و ذلك قول الله: { وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ } - قال-: توحيدهم لله

sources.gloss: That is God's word, ‘to Him submits whoever there is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be brought back’. He said: their affirming God's oneness.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وفي المجمع عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام ان الله تعالى أخذ الميثاق على الأنبياء قبل نبيّنا ان يخبروا اممهم بمبعثه ونعته ويبشّروهم به ويأمروهم بتصديقه

sources.gloss: In al-Majma, from Amir al-Muminin: God took the compact upon the prophets before our Prophet that they should tell their communities of his mission and his description, give them glad tidings of him, and command them to affirm him.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: لعل المراد ان ذلك في زمان القائم عليه السلام كما رواه العياشي عنه عليه السلام انها نزلت في القائم عليه السلام. وفي رواية تلاها فقال إذا قام القائم عليه الصلاة والسلام لا يبقى ارض الاَّ نودي فيها شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وان محمداً رسول الله

sources.gloss: Perhaps what is meant is that this is in the time of the Qaim, as al-Ayyashi narrated from him that it came down about the Qaim. And in a report he recited it and said: when the Qaim rises, no land will be left without the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God being proclaimed in it.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وقال طاوس والحسن البصري وقتادة أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين أن يصدق بعضهم بعضاً، وهذا لا يضاد ما قاله علي وابن عباس، ولا ينفيه، بل يستلزمه ويقتضيه

sources.gloss: Tawus, al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatada said: God took the compact of the prophets that they affirm one another. This does not contradict what Ali and Ibn Abbas said, nor does it deny it; rather it entails it and requires it.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: فاتقوا الله في سرائركم وعلانيتكم ولا تموتن الا وأنتم مسلمون

sources.gloss: So fear God in your private and your public affairs, and do not die except as Muslims.

title.en: Piety, the Torah and the House

essay.en:
"You will never attain piety until you spend out of what you hold dear." Tusi ties the verse to the one before it, where a whole earth of gold ransoms no one who dies faithless, so that the uselessness of ransom would not slacken anyone in charity [10]. Tabrisi records the old disagreement over what piety, birr, names here: Paradise, from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid; obedience and God-fearing, from Muqatil and Ata; or "you will not be righteous", from al-Hasan [4]. Tabatabai keeps the word at its lexical width, expansiveness in doing good, and reads spending what one loves as one pillar of the birr that 2:177 sets out [1].

The argument then turns to food.
