When one of them sinned, the expiation of his sin would be found written on the threshold of his door: cut off your nose or your ear, do such and such. The Messenger of God was silent, and the verse was revealed.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { سنن } من الله في الأَمم السالفة إذا كذبوا رسلـه وجحدوا نبوتهم بالاستيصال وتبقية آثارهم في الديار للاعتبار والاتعاظ عن الحسن وابن إسحاق

sources.gloss: "Precedents" from God concerning the nations of the past when they belied His messengers and denied their prophethood: uprooting them, and leaving their traces in their dwellings for reflection and admonition. From al-Hasan and Ibn Ishaq.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت الآية تسلية للمؤمنين لما نالـهم يوم أحد من القتل والجراح عن الزهري وقتادة وابن أبي نجيح

sources.gloss: The verse was revealed as a consolation to the believers for the killing and the wounds that befell them on the day of Uhud. From al-Zuhri, Qatada and Ibn Abi Najih.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أنه تعالى إنما يداول بين الناس لتمحيص ذنوب المؤمنين ومحق الكافرين

sources.gloss: In this verse is an indication that He, exalted, alternates the days among people only to purge the sins of the believers and to wipe out the disbelievers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وذلك أن قوماً ممن فاتهم شهود بدر كانوا يتمنون الموت بالشهادة بعد بدر قبل أحد فلما رأوه يوم أحد أعرض كثير منهم عنه فانهزموا فعاتبهم الله على ذلك عن الحسن ومجاهد والربيع وقتادة والسدي

sources.gloss: That is because a group of those who missed being present at Badr used to long for death by martyrdom after Badr and before Uhud; and when they saw it on the day of Uhud many of them turned away from it and fled, so God reproached them for that. From al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Rabi, Qatada and al-Suddi.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والربا المنهي عنه قال عطا، ومجاهد: هو ربا الجاهلية، وهو الزيادة على أصل المال بالتأخير عن الأجل الحال

sources.gloss: As for the usury that is forbidden, Ata and Mujahid said: it is the usury of the Jahiliyya, which is the increase over the principal in return for deferring the term that has fallen due.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال ابن عباس في اليسر، والعسر، فكأنه قال في السراء بكثرة المال، والضراء بقلته

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas said: in ease and in hardship; as though He said: in prosperity, with abundance of wealth, and in adversity, with its scarcity.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا حفصاً { قرح } بضم القاف. والباقون بفتحها. والفرق بينهما أن القرح - بفتح القاف - الجراح، والقرح - بالضم - ألم الجراح على قول أكثر المفسرين

sources.gloss: The people of Kufa except Hafs read qurh with u on the qaf, and the rest read it with a. The difference between them is that qarh, with a on the qaf, is the wounds, while qurh, with u, is the pain of the wounds, according to most of the commentators.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فأراهم الله إياه في يوم أحد فلم يثبتوا إلا من شاء الله منهم

sources.gloss: So God showed it to them on the day of Uhud, and they did not stand firm except those of them whom God willed.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فقال علي (عليه السلام): " كذلك الجنان تكون في علم الله تعالى "

sources.gloss: Ali said: Likewise the gardens are in the knowledge of God, exalted.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ما من عبد كظم غيظا إلا زاده الله عز و جل عزا في الدنيا و الآخرة

sources.gloss: No servant suppresses anger but that God, mighty and glorious, increases him in honour in this world and the next.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الإصرار هو أن يذنب الذنب فلا يستغفر الله، و لا يحدث نفسه بتوبة، فذلك الإصرار

sources.gloss: Persistence is that a man commits the sin and does not ask God's forgiveness and does not speak to himself of repentance. That is persistence.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و الله لتمحصن، و الله لتميزن، و الله لتغربلن حتى لا يبقى منكم إلا الأندر

sources.gloss: By God, you shall surely be purged; by God, you shall surely be distinguished; by God, you shall surely be winnowed, until none of you remains but the andar.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله هو أعلم بما هو مكونه قبل أن يكونه، و هم ذر، و علم من يجاهد ممن لا يجاهد

sources.gloss: God knows best what He will bring into being before He brings it into being, when they are motes, and He knew who would fight from who would not.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: قال عنى بذلك انظروا في القرآن فاعلموا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلكم وما أخبركم عنه

sources.gloss: He said: By this He meant, look into the Quran and learn how was the end of those before you and what He has told you about it.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: أن ناساً من الـيهود سألوا عمر بن الـخطاب عن جنة عرضها السموات والأرض، أين النار؟ قال: «أرأيتـم إذا جاء اللـيـل أين يكون النهار؟» فقالوا: اللهمّ نزعْتَ مثله من التوراة

sources.gloss: Some people of the Jews asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about a garden as vast as the heavens and the earth: where then is the Fire? He said: Tell me, when the night comes, where is the day? They said: By God, you have drawn its like out of the Torah.

sources.author: Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti

excerpt.text: إنك كتبت تدعوني إلى { جنة عرضها السماوات والأرض أعدت للمتقين } فأين النار؟ فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سبحان الله...! فأين الليل إذا جاء النهار؟

sources.gloss: You wrote inviting me to a garden as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the Godwary; where then is the Fire? The Messenger of God said: Glory be to God! Where is the night when the day comes?

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: فقال الوسواس الخناس: أنا لها. قال: بماذا؟ قال: أعدهم وأمنيهم حتى يواقعوا الخطيئة، فإذا واقعوا الخطيئة أنسيتهم الاستغفار

sources.gloss: The slinking whisperer said: I will take it on. He said: By what? He said: I promise them and raise their hopes until they fall into sin, and when they fall into sin I make them forget to seek forgiveness.

title.en: If he dies or is slain

essay.en:
These verses close the account of Uhud. Tabatabai reads them as the completion of the address that began 'O you who have faith', the earlier commands serving as a preface to these, which carry the heart of what is intended: command, prohibition, praise and rebuke [1]. Tabrisi gives the occasion. When it was cried at Uhud that the Prophet had been killed, some said, 'Had he been a prophet he would not have been killed', others said, 'We fight for what he fought for until we join him', and some turned back; the rout had begun when the archers left their post [2].

Against that panic the verse sets a plain fact. Messengers passed before him, and they died and some were killed; and it is said the point is that their followers did not apostatize at their prophets' death, so follow them [2]. Tusi reads the question as one of denial, and turning back on the heels as apostasy [5].

The next verse steadies the fear of dying. Tusi records two reasons for it: consolation for the Prophet's death, and urging on to fight, since none dies except by God's leave [6]. Wanting the reward of this world, Fayd Kashani adds, glances at those whom the spoils distracted [16].

Then the precedent: godly men who did not falter. Ribbiyyun is read as scholars and jurists, as great multitudes, and as ten thousand, that last from al-Zajjaj and narrated from Abu Jafar [4]. Their whole speech was one prayer, and it is answered in both worlds.

narrations.speaker: Hudhayfa
narrations.arabic: فلمّا رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ما قد نزل بالناس من الهزيمة والبلاء رفع البيضة عن رأسه وجعل ينادي: أيّها الناس أنا لم أمت ولم أقتل
narrations.chain: Furat, from Abu al-Qasim ibn Jamal al-Simsar, by an unbroken chain, from Hudhayfa al-Yamani

text.en: When the Messenger of God saw the rout and the affliction that had come upon the people, he lifted the helmet from his head and began to call out: O people, I have not died and I have not been killed.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: و الله لا ننقلب على أعقابنا بعد إذ هدانا الله و لئن مات أو قتل لأقاتلن على ما قاتل عليه حتى أموت، و الله إني لأخوه و ابن عمه و وارثه، فمن أحق به مني؟
narrations.chain: Amali al-Shaykh, by his chain from Ibn Abbas, that Ali used to say this in the lifetime of the Messenger of God

text.en: By God, we will not turn back on our heels after God has guided us. If he dies or is slain I will fight for what he fought for until I die. By God, I am his brother, his cousin and his heir; who has better right to him than I?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: كان الناس أهل ردة بعد النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله) إلا ثلاثة … المقداد بن الأسود، و أبو ذر الغفاري، و سلمان الفارسي (رحمة الله و بركاته عليهم)، ثم عرف أناس بعد يسير
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, by his chain from Hannan, from his father, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The people were people of apostasy after the Prophet except three ... al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari and Salman al-Farisi; then, a little later, others came to know.

note.en: Al-Jubbai read the verse as proof that a person has one appointed term only, the time at which he dies; Tusi judged that the stronger view [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أنه أصاب علياً عليه السلام يوم أُحد ستون جراحة … فقال علي عليه السلام الحمد لله إذ لم أفر ولم أُول الدبر فشكر الله له ذلك في موضعين من القرآن وهو قوله وسيجزي الله الشاكرين وسنجزي الشاكرين

text.en: Sixty wounds befell Ali on the day of Uhud ... Ali said: Praise be to God, for I did not flee and did not turn my back. So God thanked him for that in two places in the Quran: 'soon Allah will reward the grateful' and 'soon We will reward the grateful'.

note.en: The Basrans, Ibn Kathir and Nafi read qutila, was slain, the reading of Ibn Abbas; the rest read qatala, fought, the reading of Ibn Masud [4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنه سمع أبا عبد الله جعفر بن محمد (عليهما السلام) يقرأ: " و كاين من نبي قتل معه ربيون كثير " قال: " ألوف و ألوف- ثم قال- إي و الله يقتلون "
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Mansur ibn al-Sayqal

text.en: He heard Abu Abdillah Jafar ibn Muhammad recite: 'and how many a prophet was slain, and with him many godly men'. He said: Thousands upon thousands. Then he said: Yes, by God, they are slain.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: بين الله سبحانه أنه لو كان قتل صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم كما أرجف بذلك يوم أُحد لما أوجب ذلك أن يضعفوا ويهنوا كما لم يهن من كان مع الأنبياء بقتلهم

text.en: God has made clear that had he been slain, as was rumoured on the day of Uhud, that would not have obliged them to weaken or falter, just as those who were with the prophets did not falter when they were slain.

note.en: Tusi glosses excess as passing the measure wisdom requires, and says firmness of foot, though the servants' own act, is asked of God because it comes by His help [8].

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: قوله تعالى: { وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ } إلى قوله: { فِيۤ أَمْرِنَا } يعنون خطاياهم

text.en: On His words 'All that they said was', down to 'our excesses in our affairs': they mean their errors.

note.en: Tusi refers 'He gave them' to the godly men just described [9]; Fayd Kashani reads the world's reward as victory, spoils and good repute, and the hereafter's, singled out as fair, as the Garden [17].

perspectives.en: Both traditions place verse 144 after the rumour at Uhud, but they part over who the grateful are. Al-Tabari transmits from Ali that they are those steadfast in their religion, Abu Bakr and his companions, and that Abu Bakr was the most grateful of them [19]; Qurtubi records Abu Bakr mounting the pulpit and reciting the verse on the day the Prophet died [25]. The Shia blocks read it forward: al-Baqir says God thanked Ali in both places for not fleeing at Uhud [16], and al-Burhan takes the turning back on the heels as what followed the Prophet's death [12].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الآيات كما ترى تتمة للآيات السابقة المبتدئة بقوله { يا أيُّها الذين آمنوا } كما أن الآيات السابقة بأوامرها ونواهيها توطئة لهذه الآيات التي تشتمل على أصل المقصود من أمر ونهي وثناء وتوبيخ

sources.gloss: These verses, as you see, complete the preceding verses that began with 'O you who have faith', just as those preceding verses, with their commands and prohibitions, are a preface to these verses, which contain the heart of what is intended: command, prohibition, praise and rebuke.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لما أُرْجف بأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد قتل يوم أحد وأشيع ذلك قال أناس لو كان نبياً لما قتل، وقال آخرون نقاتل على ما قاتل عليه حتى نلحق به، وارتد بعضهم وانهزم بعضهم … وكان سبب انهزامهم وتضعضعهم إخلال الرماة لمكانهم من الشعب … وقيل أراد أن أصحاب الأنبياء لم يرتدّوا عند موتهم أو قتلـهم فاقتدوا بهم

sources.gloss: When it was rumoured that the Prophet had been killed on the day of Uhud and this spread, some said, 'Had he been a prophet he would not have been killed', and others said, 'We fight for what he fought for until we join him'; some of them apostatized and some fled ... The cause of their rout and collapse was the archers abandoning their place in the pass ... And it is said the meaning is that the companions of the prophets did not apostatize at their death or killing, so follow them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقرأ أهل البصرة وابن كثير ونافع قُتل بضم القاف بغير ألف وهي قراءة ابن عباس والباقون قاتل بالألف وهي قراءة ابن مسعود … وقيل في ربيّون أقوال أحدها: أنهم علماء فقهاء صبر عن ابن عباس والحسن وثانيها: أنهم جموع كثيرة عن مجاهد وقتادة … أن الربيين عشرة آلاف عن الزجاج وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر

sources.gloss: The people of Basra, Ibn Kathir and Nafi read 'qutila', with a damma and no alif, which is the reading of Ibn Abbas; the rest read 'qatala', with an alif, the reading of Ibn Masud ... On ribbiyyun there are several views: that they are scholars, jurists and steadfast men, from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan; that they are great multitudes, from Mujahid and Qatada ... that the ribbiyyun are ten thousand, from al-Zajjaj, and that is what is narrated from Abu Jafar.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والالف في قوله: { أفان } ألف انكار بصورة ألف استفهام … ومعنى { انقلبتم على أعقابكم } أي ارتددتم كفاراً بعد إيمانكم

sources.gloss: The alif in His words 'What then, if' is an alif of denial in the form of an interrogative alif ... and the meaning of 'you turned back on your heels' is: you apostatized as disbelievers after your faith.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أحدهما - التسلية عما يلحق النفس بموت النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) من جهة أنه باذن الله عز وجل … الثاني - للحض على الجهاد من حيث لا يموت أحد إلا باذن الله تعالى … وقال الجبائي في الآية دلالة على أن اجل الانسان إنما هو أجل واحد … والأقوى الأول

sources.gloss: The first is consolation for what befalls the soul at the death of the Prophet, in that it is by God's leave ... The second is to urge on to jihad, since no one dies except by God's leave ... Al-Jubbai said the verse indicates that a person's term is a single term ... and the first view is the stronger.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فالاسراف هو مجاوزة المقدار الذي تقتضيه الحكمة … وقوله: { وثبت أقدامنا } أي أعنا وألطف لنا بما تثبت معه أقدامنا وإن كان ثبوت القدم من فعل العباد لكن لما كان بلطفه ومعونته جاز نسبته إليه مجازا

sources.gloss: Excess is passing the measure that wisdom requires ... And His words 'make our feet steady' mean: help us and be gracious to us with that by which our feet stay steady; and though firmness of foot is an act of the servants, since it is by His grace and help it may be ascribed to Him figuratively.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قوله: { فآتاهم الله } يعني من تقدم ذكره من الربيين الذين وصفهم

sources.gloss: His words 'So Allah gave them' mean those mentioned before, the godly men whom He described.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: كان الناس أهل ردة بعد النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله) إلا ثلاثة

sources.gloss: The people were people of apostasy after the Prophet except three.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أنه سمع أبا عبد الله جعفر بن محمد (عليهما السلام) يقرأ: " و كاين من نبي قتل معه ربيون كثير " قال: " ألوف و ألوف- ثم قال- إي و الله يقتلون "

sources.gloss: He heard Abu Abdillah Jafar ibn Muhammad recite, 'and how many a prophet was slain, and with him many godly men'. He said: Thousands upon thousands. Then he said: Yes, by God, they are slain.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قوله تعالى: { وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ } إلى قوله: { فِيۤ أَمْرِنَا } يعنون خطاياهم

sources.gloss: His words 'All that they said was', down to 'our excesses in our affairs': they mean their errors.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: { وَمَنْ يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا } تعريض بمن شغلته الغنائم يوم أُحد

sources.gloss: 'Whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him of it' is an allusion to those whom the spoils occupied on the day of Uhud.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: فأتاهم الله بسبب الإِستغفار واللجأ إلى الله النصر والغنيمة وحسن الذكر في الدنيا والجنة والنعيم في الآخرة وخص ثواب الآخرة بالحسن اشعاراً بفضله

sources.gloss: So God gave them, by reason of their seeking forgiveness and taking refuge in God, victory, spoils and good repute in this world, and the Garden and its bliss in the hereafter; and He singled out the reward of the hereafter as fair, to signal its excellence.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: فلمّا رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ما قد نزل بالناس من الهزيمة والبلاء رفع البيضة عن رأسه وجعل ينادي: أيّها الناس أنا لم أمت ولم أقتل

sources.gloss: When the Messenger of God saw the rout and the affliction that had come upon the people, he lifted the helmet from his head and began to call out: O people, I have not died and I have not been killed.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: عن علـيّ فـي قوله: { وَسَيَجْزِى ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّـٰكِرِينَ }: الثابتـين علـى دينهم أبـا بكر وأصحابه

sources.gloss: From Ali, on His words 'and soon Allah will reward the grateful': those steadfast in their religion, Abu Bakr and his companions.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: فقام أبو بكر فصعِد المنبر فقال: من كان يعبد الله فإن الله حيٌّ لم يمت، ومن كان يعبد محمداً فإن محمداً قد مات

sources.gloss: Abu Bakr rose and mounted the pulpit and said: whoever worshipped God, God is living and has not died; and whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died.

essay.en:
The passage returns to Uhud and to the voices heard after it. 'If you obey the faithless, they will turn you back on your heels': al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj read the faithless as the Jews and Christians whose advice was not to be taken, while al-Suddi read them as Abu Sufyan and his men [7]. Against every such voice the verse sets one name: Allah is your Master, and He is the best of helpers.

Then a promise. Terror will be cast into the hearts of the faithless. Al-Suddi tells how Abu Sufyan's men, already on the road to Mecca, resolved to turn back and wipe the Muslims out, until God cast that terror into their hearts and they gave up what they had intended [3].

Verse 152 audits the day. God kept His promise while the archers held their ground; then they fell to arguing, some asking what they were still standing there for, others refusing to go against the Prophet's command, and the rest ran off to plunder [21]. Tabatabai insists their failure was one of judgment rather than nerve: what moved them was appetite for the spoils, not fear [1]. What follows is the flight, with the Prophet's voice behind them, and then a sleep sent down on one group while another lay awake with the thoughts of pagan ignorance. The passage ends not in a sentence but in a pardon.

note.en: Al-Qummi names the caller Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who marched out with the Messenger of God and then turned back, making his companions lose heart [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: نزلت في المنافقين إذ قالوا للمؤمنين يوم أُحد عند الهزيمة ارجعوا إلى اخوانكم وارجعوا إلى دينهم
narrations.chain: In al-Majma, from Amir al-Muminin

text.en: It came down about the hypocrites, when they said to the believers on the day of Uhud, at the rout: go back to your brothers, and go back to their religion.

note.en: 'Master' here means that He has the better claim on your obedience and the better claim to help you [2].
'Authority' here means proof and argument; al-Tusi reads the phrase as a verdict on blind imitation, since whoever holds a doctrine without proof stands refuted by it [8].

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: نصرت بالرعب مسيرة شهر
narrations.chain: In al-Majma, from the Prophet

text.en: I have been helped by terror over the distance of a month's journey.

note.en: Al-Qummi glosses 'some among you desire this world' as the men who left their post for the spoils, and those who desire the Hereafter as Abdullah ibn Jubayr and those who stayed until killed [15].

narrations.speaker: Ibn Masud
narrations.arabic: ما كنت أدري أن أحداً من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يريد الدنيا حتى نزلت فينا هذه الآية يوم أحد

text.en: I did not know that any of the companions of the Messenger of God desired this world until this verse came down about us on the day of Uhud.

note.en: 'The Apostle was calling you from your rear': he was calling out from behind them, come back to me, servants of God, come back to me, I am the Messenger of God [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فأما الغم الأول فالهزيمة والقتل، وأما الغم الآخر فإشراف خالد بن الوليد عليهم … { لكيلا تحزنوا على ما فاتكم } من الغنيمة { ولا ما أصابكم } يعني قتل إخوانهم
narrations.chain: In the narration of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The first grief was the rout and the killing; the other grief was Khalid ibn al-Walid looming over them. 'So that you may not grieve for what you lose' means the spoils, 'nor for what befalls you' means the killing of their brothers.

narrations.speaker: Ibn Abbas
narrations.arabic: فلم يبق معه من الناس غير علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام ورجل من الأنصار فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: يا علي قد صنع الناس ما ترى! … فحمل عليها ففضها، فقال جبرئيل عليه السلام يا رسول الله إن هذه لهي المواساة
narrations.chain: Furat, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf, by an'ana, from al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn Abbas

text.en: No one of the people remained with him but Ali ibn Abi Talib and a man of the Ansar. The Prophet said: Ali, the people have done what you see. He charged the squadron and broke it, and Gabriel said: Messenger of God, this is true self-sacrifice.

note.en: The wounded came back making their excuses, and God sent down the sleep that told the truthful from the liar: the believers dropped where they stood while the hypocrites could not settle [16].

narrations.speaker: Ibn Abbas
narrations.arabic: نزلت في علي [بن أبي طالب عليه السلام.ن] غشيه النعاس يوم أحد
narrations.chain: Furat, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hakam, from Hasan ibn Husayn, from Habban, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas

text.en: It came down about Ali ibn Abi Talib: drowsiness came over him on the day of Uhud.

note.en: Al-Tusi finds here a refutation of those who trace sins to God, since the verse lays the slip on Satan [12]. Al-Qummi glosses 'some of what they had earned' as their sins [17].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: { إِنَّمَا ٱسْتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ بِبَعْضِ مَا كَسَبُواْ } … هم أصحاب العقبة
narrations.chain: Al-Ayyashi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: On 'only Satan had made them stumble because of some of their deeds': they are the companions of al-Aqaba.

perspectives.en: The traditions differ over who fled and what it cost them. Al-Tabari reports Umar reciting this verse in a Friday sermon and saying that at Uhud he fled until he had climbed the mountain, leaping like a mountain goat [32]. Al-Qurtubi weighs whether the retreat was a sin at all, and settles it either way: if it was a real sin God pardoned it, and if it was a permitted withdrawal the verse concerns those who went too far [40]. Al-Balkhi, cited by al-Tabrisi, counts only thirteen men left with the Prophet, and among the Muhajirun only Ali and Talha beyond dispute [6].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وعلى هذا فلا بد من تفسير الفشل بضعف الرأي وأما كونه بمعنى الجبن فلا ينطبق عليهم إذ لم يكن ذلك منهم جبناً بل طمعاً في الغنيمة

sources.gloss: On this reading, fashal must be explained as weakness of judgment; taking it to mean cowardice does not fit them, since what they did was not out of cowardice but out of greed for the spoils.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { بل الله مولاكم } أي لـهو أولى بأن تطيعوه وهو أولى بنصرتكم

sources.gloss: 'Indeed, Allah is your Master': that is, He has the better claim that you obey Him, and the better claim to help you.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال السدي لما ارتحل أبو سفيان والمشركون يوم أحد متوجهين إلى مكة قالوا بئس ما صنعنا قتلناهم حتى إذا لم يبق منهم إلا الشريد تركناهم ارجعوا فاستأصلوهم فلما عزموا على ذلك ألقى الله في قلوبـهم الرعب حتى رجعوا عما هموّا به

sources.gloss: Al-Suddi said: when Abu Sufyan and the polytheists set out on the day of Uhud heading for Mecca, they said: how badly we have done. We killed them until none was left but stragglers, then we left them. Go back and wipe them out. When they resolved on that, God cast terror into their hearts, so that they turned back from what they had intended.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وروي عن ابن مسعود قال ما كنت أدري أن أحداً من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يريد الدنيا حتى نزلت فينا هذه الآية يوم أحد

sources.gloss: It is related from Ibn Masud that he said: I did not know that any of the companions of the Messenger of God desired this world until this verse came down about us on the day of Uhud.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { يدعوكم في أخراكم } أي يناديكم من ورائكم فيقول ارجعوا إليّ عبادَ الله ارجعوا إليَّ أنا رسول الله

sources.gloss: 'Calling you from your rear': that is, calling out to you from behind you, saying: come back to me, servants of God, come back to me, I am the Messenger of God.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وذكر أبو القاسم البلخي أنه لم يبق مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم أحد إلا ثلاثة عشر نفساً خمسة من المهاجرين وثمانية من الأنصار فأما المهاجرون فعلي ع وأبو بكر وطلحة وعبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن أبي وقاص وقد اختلف في الجميع إلا في علي ع وطلحة

sources.gloss: Abu al-Qasim al-Balkhi mentioned that only thirteen men remained with the Prophet on the day of Uhud, five of the Muhajirun and eight of the Ansar. As for the Muhajirun, they were Ali, Abu Bakr, Talha, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, and there is dispute over all of them except Ali and Talha.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الحسن، وابن جريج إنهم اليهود، والنصارى أي إن تستنصحوهم وتقبلوا رأيهم يردوكم خاسرين. وقال السدي: أراد إن تطيعوا أبا سفيان وأصحابه يرجعوكم كافرين

sources.gloss: Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj said they are the Jews and the Christians: that is, if you take their counsel and accept their opinion they will turn you back as losers. And al-Suddi said: it means, if you obey Abu Sufyan and his companions they will turn you back as disbelievers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على فساد التقليد، لأنه لا برهان مع صاحبه على صحة مذهبه، فكل من قال بمذهب لا برهان عليه، فمبطل بدلالة الآية

sources.gloss: In the verse is an indication of the corruption of blind imitation, since its holder has no proof for the soundness of his school; so everyone who holds a doctrine with no proof for it is in the wrong, by the verse's indication.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دليل على فساد قول المجبرة: من أن المعاصي من الله، لأنه تعالى نسب ذلك في الآية إلى استزلال الشيطان

sources.gloss: In the verse is proof of the falsity of the Mujbira's claim that acts of disobedience are from God, since God attributed that in the verse to Satan's making them slip.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني عبدالله بن أبي حيث خرج مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله ثم رجع يجبن أصحابه

sources.gloss: It means Abdullah ibn Ubayy, when he went out with the Messenger of God and then turned back, making his companions lose heart.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني أصحاب عبدالله بن جبير الذين تركوا مركزهم ومروا للغنيمة، قوله: { ومنكم من يريد الآخرة } يعني عبدالله بن جبير وأصحابه الذين بقوا حتى قتلوا

sources.gloss: It means the companions of Abdullah ibn Jubayr, who left their post and went off for the spoils; 'and some among you desire the Hereafter' means Abdullah ibn Jubayr and his companions, who stayed until they were killed.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فأنزل الله عليهم النعاس في تلك الحالة حتى كانوا يسقطون إلى الأرض وكان المنافقون الذين يكذبون لا يستقرون قد طارت عقولهم وهم يتكلمون بكلام لا يفهم عنهم

sources.gloss: So God sent drowsiness down on them in that state, until they were dropping to the ground; while the hypocrites who were lying could not stay still, their wits had flown, and they spoke words that could not be understood from them.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: { ببعض ما كسبوا } قال: بذنوبهم

sources.gloss: 'Because of some of their deeds', he said: by their sins.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هم أصحاب العقبة

sources.gloss: They are the companions of al-Aqaba.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: في المجمع عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام نزلت في المنافقين إذ قالوا للمؤمنين يوم أُحد عند الهزيمة ارجعوا إلى اخوانكم وارجعوا إلى دينهم

sources.gloss: In al-Majma, from Amir al-Muminin: it came down about the hypocrites, when they said to the believers on the day of Uhud, at the rout: go back to your brothers, and go back to their religion.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: يعني اختلاف الرماة حين انهزام المشركين فقال بعضهم فما موقفنا هيهنا وقال آخرون لا نخالف أمر الرسول فثبت مكانه أميرهم في نفر يسير ونفر الباقون للنهب

sources.gloss: It means the archers' disagreement when the polytheists were routed: some of them said, what is our standing here? and others said, we will not go against the Messenger's command. So their commander held his place with a few men, and the rest ran off to plunder.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: فلم يبق معه من الناس غير علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام ورجل من الأنصار

sources.gloss: No one of the people remained with him but Ali ibn Abi Talib and a man of the Ansar.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: نزلت في علي [بن أبي طالب عليه السلام.ن] غشيه النعاس يوم أحد

sources.gloss: It came down about Ali ibn Abi Talib: drowsiness came over him on the day of Uhud.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: لـما كان يوم أحد هزمناهم، ففررت حتـى صعدت الـجبل، فلقد رأيتنـي أنزو كأننـي أَرْوَى

sources.gloss: On the day of Uhud we routed them, then I fled until I had climbed the mountain, and I saw myself leaping as though I were a mountain goat.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وعلى الجملة فإن حُمِل الأمر على ذنب مُحَقَّق فقد عفا الله عنه، وإن حُمِل على انهزام مُسَوّغ فالآية فيمن أبْعَد في الهزيمة وزاد على القدر المسوّغ

sources.gloss: In sum: if the matter is taken as a definite sin, God has pardoned it; and if it is taken as a permitted retreat, then the verse concerns whoever went far in the flight and beyond the permitted measure.

essay.en:
These verses finish the Uhud sequence. Tabatabai reads them as answering both the regret left by so many killed and the thought underneath it, that the Messenger had brought them to this ruin [1]. The passage opens by forbidding a sentence: 'Had they stayed with us they would not have died or been killed.' Tusi reports from al-Suddi and Mujahid that these were the words of Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions, and that travelling in the land means going out for trade or a living [13]. Against that arithmetic stands another measure: forgiveness and mercy 'are surely better than what they amass', words Tusi reads against hypocrites who were holding the believers back [14].

Then the address turns to the Prophet. His gentleness is named as Allah's mercy, and he is told to pardon, to ask forgiveness, and to consult. Tabrisi records the disagreement over why a man who receives revelation should take counsel: to put his companions at ease and raise their standing, so his community would follow him, to test who advises sincerely, or because the matter is worldly and military [4]. Obedience earns Allah's help, disobedience His abandonment [5]. The charge of dishonesty is then met directly: Tabrisi reports the verse came down over a red cloak missing from the spoils of Badr, and on Muqatil's account over the archers who left their post at Uhud for the booty [6].

Two ends are then set against each other, read either of breach and its avoidance, or of the fighter and the deserter [7]; then comes the favour of an apostle from among themselves [8]. Only now does the Quran answer 'How is this?' Tabrisi records three readings of 'from your own souls': the insistence on marching out of Medina, the ransom taken for the captives of Badr, narrated from Ali and al-Baqir, and the archers' breach [9]. Tabatabai names disobedience to the Messenger, failure of nerve and dispute as the cause of the rout [2]. 'By Allah's permission' cannot mean licence, for Allah does not make sins lawful [10]. Those who sat back are told to keep death from themselves if they can [11]. The slain are not dead: living, provided for, rejoicing, and alive now, Tusi insists, since life in the barzakh is within Allah's power [26]. al-Baqir, Tabrisi reports, held that the verse takes in the slain of Badr and Uhud together [12].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أ تدري ما سبيل الله … سبيل الله: علي (عليه السلام) و ذريته، من قتل في ولايته قتل في سبيل الله، و من مات في ولايته مات في سبيل الله
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from al-Munakhkhal, from Jabir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: 'Do you know what the way of Allah is?' Jabir said no. He said: 'The way of Allah is Ali and his progeny. Whoever is slain under his wilaya is slain in the way of Allah, and whoever dies under his wilaya dies in the way of Allah.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: لا، الموت موت، و القتل قتل … ليس من قتل بالسيف كمن مات على فراشه، إن من قتل لا بد أن يرجع إلى الدنيا حتى يذوق الموت
narrations.chain: Sad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riab, from Zurara

text.en: Asked whether one who is slain has died, he said: 'No. Death is death and being slain is being slain.' The Book keeps them apart: 'If you die or are slain.' One killed by the sword is not like one who dies in his bed; the slain must return to the world until he tastes death.

note.en: Qummi glosses 'they would have surely scattered' as: they would have broken and not stood with you, and calls the commands that follow a discipline for the Messenger [30].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: نعم، أقبل، إن لم أقبل كان إبطال ما يقول هذا و أصحابه- و أشار إلي بيده- و مصداق ما يقول الآخرون- يعني المخالفين- قال الله لنبيه (صلى الله عليه و آله): { فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظّاً غَلِيظَ ٱلْقَلْبِ لاَنْفَضُّواْ مِنْ حَوْلِكَ فَٱعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي ٱلأَمْرِ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Safwan

text.en: Asked to accept a man's apology, he said: 'Yes, I accept. Were I not to accept, it would nullify what this man and his companions say. Allah said to His Prophet: It is by Allah's mercy that you are gentle to them, so excuse them and plead for forgiveness for them, and consult them in the affairs.'

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: لا وحدة أوحش من العجب ولا مظاهرة أوثق من المشاورة

text.en: There is no loneliness more desolate than conceit, and no support more trustworthy than consultation.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إذا فعل العبد ما أمره الله عز وجل به من الطاعة كان فعله وفقا لأمر الله عز وجل وسمي العبد به موفقا … ومتى خلى بينه وبين تلك المعصية فلم يحل بينه وبينها حتى يرتكبها فقد خذله ولم ينصره ولم يوفقه
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani and Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq, from Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan, from Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, from Tamim ibn Bahlul, from his father, from Jafar ibn Sulayman al-Basri, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi

text.en: When the servant does what Allah commanded him of obedience, his act accords with Allah's command and the servant is called one given success. Whenever Allah leaves him to a sin and does not come between him and it until he commits it, He has forsaken him, not helped him and not given him success.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ألم ينسبوا نبينا محمدا (صلى الله عليه و آله) إلى أنه يوم بدر أخذ [لنفسه] من المغنم قطيفة حمراء، حتى أظهره الله عز و جل على القطيفة، و برأ نبيه (صلى الله عليه و آله) من الخيانة، و أنزل في كتابه: { وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ وَمَن يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ }؟!
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Nuh ibn Shuayb, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Alqama

text.en: Did they not accuse our Prophet Muhammad of taking a red cloak for himself from the spoils on the day of Badr, until Allah brought the cloak to light and cleared His Prophet of treachery, and sent down in His Book: 'A prophet may not breach his trust'?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وصدق الله لم يكن الله ليجعل نبياً غالاً { ومن يغلل يأت بما غل يوم القيامة } ومن غل شيئاً رآه يوم القيامة في النار ثم يكلف أن يدخل إليه فيخرجه من النار
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Allah spoke truly: Allah would not make a prophet one who breaches trust. Whoever took anything by breach will see it on the Day of Resurrection in the Fire, then be charged to go in to it and bring it out of the Fire.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا رِضْوَانَ الله هُمُ الائِمَّةُ وَهُمْ وَالله يَا عَمَّارُ دَرَجَاتٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَبِوَلايَتِهِمْ وَمَعْرِفَتِهِمْ إِيَّانَا يُضَاعِفُ الله لَهُمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ وَيَرْفَعُ الله لَهُمُ الدَّرَجَاتِ الْعُلَى.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati

text.en: Those who followed Allah's pleasure are the Imams. They, by Allah, O Ammar, are ranks for the believers: by loyalty to them and by their knowing us, Allah multiplies their deeds for them and raises them the highest ranks.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: الدرجة ما بين السماء إلى الأرض

text.en: Recalling Allah's words 'They have ranks with Allah', he said: the rank is what lies between heaven and earth.

note.en: Tabrisi gives three senses of 'from among themselves': from their own clan, who knew his upbringing and honesty; that he speaks their tongue; or that he is of their own kind, no angel or jinn [8].
Tabrisi reports that Abdullah ibn Ubayy and the hypocrites with him, some three hundred, withdrew at Uhud, and that Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram called after them to fight or to defend [10].
Tabrisi reads 'their brethren' as brothers in lineage, not in religion, and answers that they cannot ward off death: an enemy might have come in and killed them inside their own houses [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هم والله شيعتنا إذا دخلوا الجنة واستقبلوا الكرامة من الله استبشروا بمن لم يلحق بهم من إخوانهم من المؤمنين في الدنيا
narrations.chain: his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: They are, by Allah, our Shia. When they enter the Garden and receive Allah's honouring, they rejoice for those of their brethren among the believers in this world who have not yet joined them.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.addressee: a man who came to him
narrations.arabic: أتى رجل رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) فقال: إني راغب نشيط في الجهاد في سبيل الله قال: فجاهد في سبيل الله، فإنك إن تقتل كنت حيا عند الله ترزق، و إن مت فقد وقع أجرك على الله، و إن رجعت خرجت من الذنوب إلى الله
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Jabir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: A man said: I am eager and keen for jihad in the way of Allah. He said: 'Then fight in the way of Allah. If you are killed you are living with Allah, provided for; if you die, your reward has fallen due upon Allah; and if you return, you come out of your sins.'

perspectives.en: The traditions part over two lines. On 'consult them in the affairs', al-Suyuti transmits from Ibn Abbas that the ones meant are Abu Bakr and Umar [90], while Tabrisi reports a disagreement over the purpose of the consultation: to put the companions at ease, to set a precedent for the community, to test who advises sincerely, or to canvass opinion in worldly and military affairs [4]. On 'Is he who follows Allah's pleasure', al-Tabari prefers al-Dahhak's reading, contrasting the man who kept clear of breach of trust with the man who committed it [53]; the narrations from the Imams read those who follow His pleasure as the Imams, and the ranks as the believers' through loyalty to them [99].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وبالجملة الآيات تبين ما في هذا الأسف والحسرة من الخطأ والخبط وتعطف على أمر آخر يستتبعه هذا الأسف والتحسر وهو سوء ظنهم برسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأنه هو الذي أوردهم هذا المورد وألقاهم في هذه التهلكة

sources.gloss: In sum, the verses show the error and confusion in this sorrow and regret, and turn to something else that follows from it: their ill thought about the Messenger of Allah, that it was he who brought them to this pass and cast them into this ruin.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وبالجملة سببه معصيتهم الرسول - وهو قائدهم - وفشلهم وتنازعهم في الأمر وذلك سبب للانهزام بحسب سنة الطبيعة والعادة.

sources.gloss: In sum, its cause was their disobedience to the Messenger, who was their commander, and their failure of nerve and their dispute in the matter, and that is a cause of rout by the ordinary law of nature and custom.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: واختلفوا في فائدة مشاورته إياهم مع استغنائه بالوحي عن تعرف صواب الرأي من العباد على أقوال أحدها: أن ذلك على وجه التطييب لنفوسهم والتألف لـهم والرفع من أقدارهم ليبين أنهم ممن يوثق بأقوالـهم ويرجع إلى آرائهم عن قتادة والربيع وابن إسحاق وثانيها: إن ذلك لتقتدي به أمته في المشاورة ولم يروها نقيصة كما مدحوا بأن أمرهم شورى بينهم عن سفيان بن عيينة وثالثها: أن ذلك لأمرين لإجلال أصحابه ولتقتدي أمته في ذلك عن الحسن والضحاك ورابعها: أن ذلك ليمتحنهم بالمشاورة ليتميز الناصح من الغاش وخامسها: أن ذلك في أمور الدنيا ومكائد الحرب ولقاء العدو وفي مثل ذلك يجوز أن يستعين بآرائهم عن أبي علي الجبائي.

sources.gloss: They disagreed about the benefit of his consulting them, given that revelation made him independent of learning sound opinion from people. First: it was to put their hearts at ease, to win them over and to raise their standing, showing that they are people whose words are trusted and whose opinions are turned to - from Qatada, al-Rabi and Ibn Ishaq. Second: so that his community would follow him in consultation and not see it as a defect. Fourth: to test them by consultation, so the sincere adviser is told apart from the deceitful. Fifth: that it concerns worldly matters, the stratagems of war and meeting the enemy, and in such things he may seek the aid of their opinions - from Abu Ali al-Jubbai.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وتضمنت الآية الترغيب في طاعة الله التي يستحق بها النصرة والتحذير من معصية الله التي يستحق بها الخذلان

sources.gloss: The verse contains encouragement toward obedience to Allah, by which one deserves His help, and warning against disobedience to Allah, by which one deserves to be forsaken.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: روي عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير أنها نزلت في قطيفة حمراء فقدت يوم بدر من المغنم فقال بعضهم لعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذها. … وعن مقاتل: أنها نزلت في غنائم أحد حين ترك الرماة المركز طلباً للغنيمة

sources.gloss: It is related from Ibn Abbas and Said ibn Jubayr that it came down over a red cloak missing from the spoils on the day of Badr, when some of them said: perhaps the Prophet took it. … And from Muqatil: that it came down over the spoils of Uhud, when the archers left their post seeking the booty.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أن معناه أفمن اتبع رضوان الله ترك الغلول كمن باء بسخط من الله في فعل الغلول عن الحسن والضحاك واختاره الطبري لأنهُ أشبه بما تقدم وثانيها: أفمن اتبع رضوان الله بالجهاد في سبيلـه { كمن باء بسخط من الله } في الفرار منه رغبة عنهُ عن الزجاج والجبائي

sources.gloss: First: its meaning is, is he who followed Allah's pleasure in leaving breach of trust like him who earned Allah's displeasure by committing breach of trust - from al-Hasan and al-Dahhak, and al-Tabari chose it. Second: is he who followed Allah's pleasure by fighting in His way like him who earned Allah's displeasure by fleeing from it - from al-Zajjaj and al-Jubbai.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { من أنفسهم } فيه أقوال أحدها: أن المراد به من رهطهم يعرفون منشأه وصدقه وأمانته وكونه أميّاً لم يكتب كتاباً ولم يقرأه ليعلموا أن ما أتى به وحي منزل ويكون ذلك شرفاً لـهم وداعياً إياهم إلى الإيمان وثانيها: أن المراد به أنه يتكلم بلسانهم فيسهل عليهم تعلم الحكمة منه فيكون خاصاً بالعرب وثالثها: أنه عام لجميع المؤمنين والمراد بأنفسهم أنه من جنسهم لم يبعث ملكاً ولا جنيا

sources.gloss: On 'from among themselves' there are several views. First: that it means from their own clan, who know his upbringing, his truthfulness and his trustworthiness, and that he was unlettered. Second: that he speaks their tongue, so learning wisdom from him is easy. Third: that it is general to all the faithful, meaning he is of their own kind: no angel or jinn was sent.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أحدها: أي ذلك بمخالفتهم الرسول في الخروج من المدينة للقتال يوم أحد … وثانيها: أن ذلك باختيارهم الفداء من الأسرى يوم بدر وكان الحكم فيهم القتل وشرط عليهم أنكم إن قبلتم الفداء قتل منكم في المقابل بعدتهم فقالوا رضينا فإنا نأخذ الفداء وننتفع به وإذا قتل منا فيما بعد كنا شهداء عن علي ع وعبيدة السلماني وهو المروي عن الباقر ع وثالثها: أن ذلك بخلاف الرماة يوم أحد

sources.gloss: First: that it was through their disagreeing with the Messenger about going out of Medina to fight on the day of Uhud. … Second: that it was through their choosing ransom for the captives on the day of Badr, when the ruling on them was death, and it was stipulated that if they accepted the ransom a like number of them would be killed the following year, and they said, we are content - from Ali and Ubayda al-Salmani, and it is what is narrated from al-Baqir. Third: that it was through the archers' breach on the day of Uhud.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ولا يجوز أن يكون المراد بالإذن ها هنا الإباحة والإطلاق كما يقتضيه اللفظ لأن الله لا يبيح المعاصي ولا يُطلقها وقتل الكافر المسلم من أعظم المعاصي فكيف يأذن فيه. … قالوا إن عبد الله بن أبي والمنافقين معه من أصحابه انخذلوا يوم أحد نحواً من ثلثمائة رجل وقالوا علامَ نقتل أنفسنا وقال لـهم عبد الله بن عمرو بن حزام الأنصاري: تعالوا قاتلوا في سبيل الله واتقوا الله ولا تخذلوا نبيكم

sources.gloss: It is not allowed that 'permission' here mean licence and leave, as the wording suggests, because Allah does not make sins lawful nor licence them. … They said that Abdullah ibn Ubayy and the hypocrites with him withdrew on the day of Uhud, about three hundred men, saying: why should we get ourselves killed? And Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram al-Ansari said to them: come, fight in the way of Allah, fear Allah, and do not fail your Prophet.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { الذين قالوا } يعني المنافقين { لإخوانهم } في النسب لا في الدين … ولا يمكنهم دفع الموت لأنه يجوز أن يدخل عليهم العدو فيقتلـهم في قعر بيوتهم

sources.gloss: 'Those who said' means the hypocrites; 'to their brethren' - brethren in lineage, not in religion. … They cannot ward off death, for the enemy might have come in upon them and killed them in the depths of their houses.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل نزلت في شهداء بدر وكانوا أربعة عشر رجلاً ثمانية من الأنصار وستة من المهاجرين، وقيل نزلت في شهداء أحد وكانوا سبعين رجلاً أربعة من المهاجرين حمزة بن عبد المطلب ومصعب بن عمير وعثمان بن شماس وعبد الله بن جحش وسائرهم من الأنصار عن ابن مسعود والربيع وقتادة وقال الباقر ع: وكثير من المفسرين أنها تتناول قتلى بدر وأحد معاً، وقيل نزلت في شهداء بئر معونة.

sources.gloss: It is said that it came down about the martyrs of Badr, who were fourteen men, eight of the Ansar and six of the Muhajirun; and it is said it came down about the martyrs of Uhud, who were seventy men. … And al-Baqir said, and many of the commentators, that it takes in the slain of Badr and Uhud together; and it is said it came down about the martyrs of Bir Mauna.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: هذا خطاب متوجه إلى المؤمنين الذين نهاهم الله أن يكونوا مثل الذين كفروا، وقالوا لأخوانهم، وهم عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول، وأصحابه - في قول السدي ومجاهد -: { إذا ضربوا في الأرض } أي سافروا فيها لتجارة أو طلب معيشة - في قول ابن اسحاق، والسدي -

sources.gloss: This is an address directed to the believers, whom Allah forbade to be like those who disbelieved and said of their brethren - and they are Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions, in the statement of al-Suddi and Mujahid - 'when they travel in the land', that is, travel in it for trade or seeking a livelihood, in the statement of Ibn Ishaq and al-Suddi.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعنى الآية أن المنافقين كانوا يثبطون المؤمنين عن الجهاد، على ما تقدم شرحه في هذه السورة فبين الله تعالى لو انكم إن قتلتم أو متم من غير أن تقتلوا { لمغفرة من الله ورحمة } تنالونهما { خير مما يجمعون } من حطام الدنيا

sources.gloss: The meaning of the verse is that the hypocrites were holding the believers back from fighting, so Allah made clear that if you are slain or die, forgiveness and mercy from Allah that you attain are better than what they amass of the perishable stuff of this world.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعنى الآية النهي عن أن يظن أحد أن المقتولين في سبيل الله أموات … لأن إحياء الله لهم في البرزخ جائز مقدور والحكمة تجيزه

sources.gloss: The meaning of the verse is the prohibition against anyone supposing that those slain in the way of Allah are dead. … For Allah's giving them life in the barzakh is possible and within His power, and wisdom allows it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال لنبيه: { فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم ولو كنت فظاً غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك } [159] أي: انهزموا ولم يقيموا معك ثم قال تأديباً لرسوله

sources.gloss: He said to His Prophet: 'It is by Allah's mercy that you are gentle to them; had you been harsh and hardhearted, they would have surely scattered from around you' - that is, they would have broken and not stood with you. Then He said, as a discipline for His Messenger.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وصدق الله لم يكن الله ليجعل نبياً غالاً { ومن يغلل يأت بما غل يوم القيامة } ومن غل شيئاً رآه يوم القيامة في النار ثم يكلف أن يدخل إليه فيخرجه من النار

sources.gloss: Allah spoke truly: Allah would not make a prophet one who breaches trust. 'And whoever breaches his trust will bring his breaches on the Day of Resurrection.' Whoever took anything by breach will see it on the Day of Resurrection in the Fire, then be charged to go in to it and bring it out of the Fire.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: هم والله شيعتنا إذا دخلوا الجنة واستقبلوا الكرامة من الله استبشروا بمن لم يلحق بهم من إخوانهم من المؤمنين في الدنيا

sources.gloss: They are, by Allah, our Shia: when they enter the Garden and receive honouring from Allah, they rejoice for those of their brethren among the believers in this world who have not joined them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: سبيل الله: علي (عليه السلام) و ذريته، من قتل في ولايته قتل في سبيل الله، و من مات في ولايته مات في سبيل الله

sources.gloss: The way of Allah is Ali, peace be upon him, and his progeny: whoever is slain under his wilaya is slain in the way of Allah, and whoever dies under his wilaya dies in the way of Allah.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نعم، أقبل، إن لم أقبل كان إبطال ما يقول هذا و أصحابه- و أشار إلي بيده- و مصداق ما يقول الآخرون

sources.gloss: Yes, I accept. Were I not to accept, it would be the nullifying of what this man and his companions say and the confirming of what the others say.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ألم ينسبوا نبينا محمدا (صلى الله عليه و آله) إلى أنه يوم بدر أخذ [لنفسه] من المغنم قطيفة حمراء، حتى أظهره الله عز و جل على القطيفة، و برأ نبيه (صلى الله عليه و آله) من الخيانة

sources.gloss: Did they not ascribe to our Prophet Muhammad that on the day of Badr he took for himself a red cloak from the spoils, until Allah made the cloak manifest and cleared His Prophet of treachery?

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الدرجة ما بين السماء إلى الأرض

sources.gloss: The rank is what lies between heaven and earth.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فجاهد في سبيل الله، فإنك إن تقتل كنت حيا عند الله ترزق، و إن مت فقد وقع أجرك على الله، و إن رجعت خرجت من الذنوب إلى الله

sources.gloss: Then fight in the way of Allah, for if you are killed you will be living with Allah, provided for; and if you die, your reward has fallen due upon Allah; and if you return, you come out of your sins to Allah.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: لا وحدة أوحش من العجب ولا مظاهرة أوثق من المشاورة

sources.gloss: There is no loneliness more desolate than conceit, and no support more trustworthy than consultation.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: عن الضحاك فـي قوله: { أَفَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ رِضْوٰنَ ٱللَّهِ } قال: من لـم يغلّ. { كَمَن بَاء بِسَخْطٍ مّنَ ٱللَّهِ }: كمن غلّ. … وأولـى التأولـين بتأويـل الآية عندي، قول الضحاك بن مزاحم لأن ذلك عقـيب وعيد الله علـى الغلول ونهيه عبـاده عنه

sources.gloss: From al-Dahhak on His words 'Is he who follows Allah's pleasure': the one who did not breach trust; 'like him who earns Allah's displeasure': like the one who breached it. … The sounder of the two interpretations of the verse, in my view, is the statement of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, because it comes right after Allah's threat concerning breach of trust and His forbidding it to His servants.

sources.author: Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti

excerpt.text: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه والبيهقي في سننه عن ابن عباس { وشاورهم في الأمر } قال: أبو بكر وعمر.

sources.gloss: al-Hakim, who graded it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from Ibn Abbas on 'and consult them in the affairs': Abu Bakr and Umar.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: إذا فعل العبد ما أمره الله عز وجل به من الطاعة كان فعله وفقا لأمر الله عز وجل وسمي العبد به موفقا

sources.gloss: When the servant does what Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, commanded him of obedience, his act is in accord with Allah's command, and by it the servant is called one given success.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا رِضْوَانَ الله هُمُ الائِمَّةُ وَهُمْ وَالله يَا عَمَّارُ دَرَجَاتٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِين

sources.gloss: Those who followed the pleasure of Allah are the Imams, and they, by Allah, O Ammar, are ranks for the believers.

essay.en:
Uhud is over and the wounds are still open. Tabatabai ties these verses to that battle, the link showing in the words "after they had been wounded" [1]. Al-Tabrisi gives the occasion: Abu Sufyan's men, already withdrawn, regretted it at al-Rawha and resolved to go back and root out what was left of the Muslims, and when word of that talk reached the Prophet he called for a pursuit, to frighten the enemy and show them strength; seventy men went out to Hamra al-Asad, eight miles from Medina [3]. Al-Tusi adds that the Prophet let no one go but those who had fought the day before, and that Jabir alone was given leave, his father having left him in charge of his sisters [9].

Both Allah and the Apostle are named, Tabatabai says, because at Uhud both had been disobeyed [1]. The great reward is then narrowed to "those of them who have been virtuous and Godwary", since answering a call is an outward act that need not carry virtue and Godwariness with it [1]; al-Tusi reads "of them" as describing the group rather than dividing it [9].

On the road the warning came: all the people have gathered against you. Al-Tusi names the man who brought it as Nuaym ibn Masud al-Ashjai, on al-Waqidi's word and as the position of Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah [10]. It only increased them in faith, and they answered, "Allah is sufficient for us." They returned untouched, the blessing read as safety and the grace as their trade [11].

Then the address turns to the Prophet. Do not grieve: al-Tabrisi calls this consolation, since their refusal to believe weighed on him, and notes that the verse ascribes the haste to them, against the determinists [5]. Respite is no kindness either; al-Tusi holds that "that they may increase in sin" is a lam of outcome and not of purpose, since God does not will what is ugly [15]. Tabatabai reads these closing verses as the summation of the Uhud passage: trial is a standing law from which neither unbeliever nor believer escapes [2].

So the passage ends where trial ends: the bad sorted from the good, no one let into the Unseen, and wealth grudged turned into a collar.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) بعث عليا (عليه السلام) في عشرة { ٱسْتَجَابُواْ للَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ مِن بَعْدِ مَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلْقَرْحُ } إلى { أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ } إنما نزلت في علي (عليه السلام)
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Salim ibn Abi Maryam, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The Messenger of Allah sent Ali out among ten men. "Those who responded to Allah and the Apostle after they had been wounded", to "a great reward": it was revealed only about Ali.

narrations.speaker: Abu Rafi
narrations.arabic: لما انصرف المشركون يوم احد بلغوا الروحاء، قالوا: لا الكواعب أردفتم، و لا محمدا قتلتم، ارجعوا. فبلغ ذلك رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) فبعث في آثارهم عليا (عليه السلام) في نفر من الخزرج، فجعل لا يرتحل المشركون من منزل إلا نزله علي (عليه السلام)، فأنزل الله تعالى: { ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَجَابُواْ للَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ مِن بَعْدِ مَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلْقَرْحُ }
narrations.chain: Ibn Shahrashub, from Abu Rafi by many routes

text.en: When the polytheists turned back at Uhud and reached al-Rawha they said, "You neither took the maidens nor killed Muhammad. Go back." The Prophet sent Ali after them with a party of Khazraj, and Ali camped at every halt they left. Then Allah revealed: "Those who responded to Allah and the Apostle."

note.en: Tabatabai reads the two crowds as different: the second are the enemy massing, the first those who spread the warning, and the wording reads as a group rather than one man [1].
Al-Tabrisi reports from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada that Satan frightens the believers by means of the disbelievers, and judges that reading the sounder [4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الموت خير للمؤمن و الكافر … لأن الله يقول: { وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِّلأَبْرَارِ } [آل عمران: 198]، و يقول: { وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لأَنْفُسِهِمْ إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ لِيَزْدَادُوۤاْ إِثْمَاً وَلَهْمُ عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Death is better for the believer and the unbeliever, because Allah says, "What is with Allah is better for the pious", and says, "Let the faithless not suppose that the respite We grant them is good for their souls."

note.en: Al-Tusi calls Ibn Ishaq's reading the most fitting: Allah opens the Unseen to none of you, but chose His Messenger by informing him of much that is hidden [16].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا تمضي الأيام و الليالي حتى ينادي مناد من السماء: يا أهل الحق اعتزلوا. يا أهل الباطل، اعتزلوا. فيعزل هؤلاء من هؤلاء، و يعزل هؤلاء من هؤلاء … كلا، إنه يقول في الكتاب: { مَّا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّىٰ يَمِيزَ ٱلْخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ajlan Abu Salih, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The days and nights will not pass until a caller calls from the sky: People of truth, stand apart. People of falsehood, stand apart. These are set apart from those. Asked whether they mix again after that call, he said: Never; Allah says in the Book, "until He has separated the bad ones from the good."

note.en: Al-Tusi glosses the heritage of the heavens and the earth: every other ownership is voided, so that what is left belongs to Allah alone [17].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا محمد، ما من أحد يمنع من زكاة ماله شيئا إلا جعل الله عز و جل ذلك يوم القيامة ثعبانا من النار مطوقا في عنقه، ينهش من لحمه حتى يفرغ من الحساب
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdallah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: O Muhammad, no one withholds anything of the zakat of his wealth but that Allah makes it, on the Day of Resurrection, a serpent of fire collared on his neck, tearing at his flesh until the reckoning is done.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الذي يمنع الزكاة يحول الله ماله يوم القيامة شجاعا من نار، له زنمتان، فيطوقه إياه، ثم يقال له: الزمه كما لزمك في الدنيا
narrations.chain: Yusuf al-Tatari, who heard Abu Jafar

text.en: The one who withholds zakat: Allah turns his wealth on the Day of Resurrection into a serpent of fire with two wattles and collars him with it, then it is said to him, cling to it as it clung to you in the world.

perspectives.en: On who is meant by those who responded, the two traditions look in different directions. The Shia reports gathered in al-Burhan put the verse on Ali: the Prophet sent him after the retreating Quraysh with a party of Khazraj, and al-Sadiq says it was revealed only about him [19]. Qurtubi relays from the two Sahih collections that Aisha told Urwa his father was among those who responded to Allah and the Apostle after they had been wounded, and that Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr volunteered among the seventy for the pursuit [37]. The occasion is the same; the named respondents are not.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ولعل ذكر الله والرسول مع جواز الاكتفاء في المقام بذكر أحد اللفظين إنما هو لكونهم في وقعة أُحد عصوا الله والرسول

sources.gloss: Perhaps Allah and the Apostle are both mentioned, though naming one of the two would have sufficed here, because at Uhud they had disobeyed both Allah and the Apostle.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وعلى ذلك فهذه الآيات بمنزلة الفذلكة لآيات أُحد يبين الله سبحانه فيها أن سنة الابتلاء والامتحان سنة جارية لا مناص عنها في كافر ولا مؤمن

sources.gloss: These verses stand as the summation of the Uhud verses, in which Allah makes clear that the law of trial and testing is a standing law from which neither unbeliever nor believer escapes.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فخرج في سبعين رجلاً حتى بلغ حمراء الأسد وهي من المدينة على ثمانية أميال

sources.gloss: He went out with seventy men until he reached Hamra al-Asad, which is eight miles from Medina.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة ويخوف المؤمنين بالكافرين

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada said: he frightens the believers by means of the disbelievers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وإنما قال ذلك على جهة التسلية لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه كان يصعب عليه كفر هؤلاء ويعظم عليه امتناعهم عن الإيمان

sources.gloss: He said this only by way of consoling His Prophet, since the unbelief of these people was hard on him and their holding back from faith weighed heavily on him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله { منهم } معناه تبيين الصفة لا التبعيض

sources.gloss: His words "of them" mean the setting out of a description, not a partition.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال الواقدي هو نعيم بن مسعود الاشجعي وهو قول أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله (ع)

sources.gloss: Al-Waqidi said he was Nuaym ibn Masud al-Ashjai, and that is the statement of Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ان النعمة العافية. والفضل: التجارة. والسوء: القتل

sources.gloss: One view is that the blessing is safety, the grace is the trade, and the harm is being killed.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معنى اللام ها هنا للعاقبة وليست بلام الغرض

sources.gloss: The sense of the lam here is outcome, and it is not the lam of purpose.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال ابن اسحاق: ولكن الله اجتبى رسوله باعلامه كثيراً من الغايبات. وهذا هو الأليق بالآية

sources.gloss: Ibn Ishaq said: rather, Allah chose His Messenger by informing him of many hidden things; and this is the most fitting for the verse.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معناه أنه يبطل ملك كل شيء إلا ملك الله

sources.gloss: It means that the ownership of everything is voided except the ownership of Allah.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إنما نزلت في علي (عليه السلام)

sources.gloss: It was revealed only about Ali.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الموت خير للمؤمن و الكافر

sources.gloss: Death is better for the believer and the unbeliever.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لا تمضي الأيام و الليالي حتى ينادي مناد من السماء: يا أهل الحق اعتزلوا. يا أهل الباطل، اعتزلوا

sources.gloss: The days and nights will not pass until a caller calls from the sky: people of truth, stand apart; people of falsehood, stand apart.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ما من أحد يمنع من زكاة ماله شيئا إلا جعل الله عز و جل ذلك يوم القيامة ثعبانا من النار مطوقا في عنقه

sources.gloss: There is no one who withholds anything of the zakat of his wealth but that Allah makes it, on the Day of Resurrection, a serpent of fire collared on his neck.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: كان أبوك من الذين استجابوا لله والرسول من بعد ما أصابهم القَرْح

sources.gloss: Your father was among those who responded to Allah and the Apostle after they had been wounded.

essay.en:
The passage opens on a sentence God overheard. Al-Tabrisi gives the occasion: when "Who is it that will lend Allah a good loan" came down, the Jews said Allah is poor, He asks a loan of us, and we are rich; the speaker was Hayy ibn Akhtab, on the word of al-Hasan and Mujahid [2]. God does not argue back. He records the remark, and records beside it their killing of the prophets, which Tabatabai takes to mean killing with knowledge and intent rather than by oversight or error [1], and answers both with "Taste the punishment of the burning." Al-Tusi notes that the men addressed had not killed a prophet themselves, so the verse shows that being pleased with a foul act ranks with doing it [9]; and on "because of what your hands have sent ahead" he reads a refutation of the determinists, since punishment falling without a prior crime would be injustice [10].

A second saying follows: no apostle is to be believed until fire consumes his offering. Al-Tabrisi reports that what the Torah laid down carried a clause, that this holds until Isa and Muhammad come, and when they come believe in them without an offering [3]. The reply is a question. Apostles did bring that very sign, and you killed them.

Then the tone turns to consolation. Al-Tusi reads "if they deny you" as comfort to the Prophet for the injury he was taking from the Jews and the polytheists [12]. Every soul tastes death, and the full wage comes only later; al-Tabrisi finds here that the least bliss of the hereafter outweighs all the bliss of this world [4]. Believers are then told what is coming: loss in property and person, much affront, and patience as the steadiest course.

The last turn is at the learned. A covenant was taken to explain the Book and not conceal it, and it was sold for a paltry gain. Those who brag about what they never did are not out of reach of punishment. And the closing line answers the first: the One who owns the heavens and the earth, al-Tusi says, is not poor [17].

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: و الله ما رأوا الله فيعلمون أنه فقير، و لكنهم رأوا أولياء الله فقراء، فقالوا: لو كان الله غنيا لأغنى أولياءه، فافتخروا على الله في الغناء.

text.en: By Allah, they did not see Allah so as to know that He is poor. Rather they saw the friends of Allah poor, and said: had Allah been rich He would have enriched His friends. So they boasted over Allah with wealth.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هم الذين يزعمون أن الإِمام يحتاج إلى ما يحملونه إليه.
narrations.chain: al-Manaqib, from al-Baqir

text.en: They are the ones who claim that the Imam has need of what they carry to him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أَمَا والله ما قتلوهم بأسيافهم ولكن أذاعوا أمرهم وأفشوا عليهم فقتلوا
narrations.chain: al-Kafi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: By Allah, they did not kill them with their swords. They broadcast their affair and exposed them, and so they were killed.

note.en: Al-Tusi reads the verse against the determinists: it shows that punishment falling on a servant without a crime he had already committed would be injustice [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: و تقول الملائكة: يا معشر الأشقياء، ادنوا فاشربوا منها، فإذا أعرضوا عنها ضربتهم الملائكة بالمقامع، و قيل لهم: { ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلْحَرِيقِ * ذٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ }
narrations.chain: al-Ikhtisas: Said ibn Janah, from Awf ibn Abd Allah al-Azdi, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Jufi, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The angels say: company of the wretched, come near and drink of it. When they turn away from it the angels strike them with iron hooks, and it is said to them, "Taste the punishment of the burning. That is because of what your hands have sent ahead."

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: إن قوما من اليهود قالوا لرسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): لن نؤمن لك حتى تأتينا بقربان تأكله النار. و كان عند بني إسرائيل طست، كانوا يقربون القربان فيضعونه في الطست، فتجيء نار فتقع فيه فتحرقه

text.en: A group of Jews said to the Messenger of Allah: we will not believe you until you bring us an offering that fire eats. The Children of Israel had a basin; they would place the offering in it, and fire would come and fall upon it and burn it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كان بين القائلين و القاتلين خمسمائة عام، فألزمهم الله القتل برضاهم ما فعلوا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from a man, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Between the ones who said this and the ones who did the killing there were five hundred years, yet Allah fastened the killing upon them because they were pleased with what those men had done.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: و قد علم أن هؤلاء لم يقتلوا، و لكن فقد كان هواهم مع الذين قتلوا، فسماهم الله تعالى قاتلين لمتابعة هواهم و رضاهم لذلك الفعل
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Samaa, who heard Abu Abdillah

text.en: He knew that these men had not killed. But their inclination was with those who killed, so Allah named them killers, for following their inclination and being pleased with that deed.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: { فإن كذبوك فقد كذب رسل من قبلك جاؤا بالبينات } هي الآيات (والزبر) وهي كتب الأنبياء بالنبوة { والكتاب المنير } الحلال والحرام.
narrations.chain: in the narration of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: "Who came with manifest signs": these are the signs. "Holy writs": the books of the prophets carrying prophethood. "An illuminating scripture": the lawful and the unlawful.

note.en: Tabatabai calls it a good argument that this verse establishes the intermediate state, since paying the full wage on the Day of Resurrection implies that some payment comes before it [1].

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: لَمّا نَزَلَت هذِهِ الآيَةُ: (إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَيِّتُونَ) قُلْتُ: يا رَبِّ اَيَمُوتُ الخَلائِقُ كُلُّهُم وَيَبقَى المَلائِكَةُ؟ فَنَزَلَت (كلُّ نَفسِ ذائِقَةُ المَوتِ ثُمَّ إِلَينا ترجَعُونَ).

text.en: When the verse "You will indeed die, and they too will die" was revealed, I said: my Lord, will all creatures die and the angels remain? Then was revealed, "Every soul shall taste death, then to Us you shall be brought back."

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: من قتل لم يذق الموت ثم قال لا بد من أن يرجع حتى يذوق الموت … من قتل ينشر حتى يموت ومن مات ينشر حتى يقتل
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Baqir

text.en: Whoever is killed has not tasted death. Then he said: he must return until he tastes death. Whoever is killed is raised again until he dies, and whoever dies is raised again until he is killed.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: لَمَّا قُبِضَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ص جَاءَ الْخَضِرُ ع فَوَقَفَ عَلَى بَابِ الْبَيْتِ وَ فِيهِ عَلِيٌّ وَ فَاطِمَةُ وَ الْحَسَنُ وَ الْحُسَيْنُ ع وَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ص قَدْ سُجِّيَ بِثَوْبِهِ فَقَالَ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَا أَهْلَ بَيْتِ مُحَمَّدٍ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَ إِنَّما تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ إِنَّ فِي اللَّهِ خَلَفاً مِنْ كُلِّ هَالِكٍ وَ عَزَاءً مِنْ كُلِّ مُصِيبَةٍ وَ دَرَكاً مِنْ كُلِّ فَائِتٍ

text.en: When the Messenger of Allah was taken, al-Khidr came and stood at the door of the house, where Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn were, and said: peace be upon you, family of Muhammad. Every soul shall taste death. In Allah is a successor for everyone who perishes and consolation for every affliction.

note.en: Al-Tabrisi reports on al-Zuhri's authority that the verse came down about Kab ibn al-Ashraf, who lampooned the Prophet and the believers and incited the polytheists against them [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: لوددت أني تركت فكلمت الناس ثلاثا، ثم قضى الله تعالى في ما أحب، و لكن عزمة من الله أن نصبر
narrations.chain: al-Numani, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Said ibn Uqda, from Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Yaqub al-Jufi, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli

text.en: I would have loved to be left free to speak to the people for three days, and then for Allah to decree concerning me what He loves. But it is a resolve from Allah that we be patient.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: في أموالكم بإخراج الزكاة، و في أنفسكم بتوطين النفس على الصبر
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from al-Qasim ibn al-Rabi al-Sahhaf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, that Ali ibn Musa wrote to him in answer to his questions

text.en: "In your possessions": by paying out the zakat. "And your souls": by settling the soul upon patience.

note.en: Al-Tabrisi holds that the verse makes plain speech about the truth obligatory and concealing it forbidden, and that this covers religion, rulings, verdicts and testimony [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وذلك أن الله أخذ ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب في محمد لتبيننه للناس إذا خرج ولا يكتمونه { فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم } يقول نبذوا عهد الله وراء ظهورهم { واشتروا به ثمناً قليلاً فبئس ما يشترون }.
narrations.chain: in the narration of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Allah took the covenant of those given the Book concerning Muhammad, that they would explain him to the people when he came forth and not conceal him. "They cast it behind their backs": they cast the covenant of Allah behind their backs.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ما أخذ الله على أهل الجهل أن يتعلموا حتى أخذ على أهل العلم أن يُعلّموا.
narrations.chain: al-Thalabi, from al-Hasan ibn Umara, from al-Hakam ibn Uyayna, from Najm al-Jazzar, who heard Ali ibn Abi Talib

text.en: Allah did not bind the people of ignorance to learn until He had bound the people of knowledge to teach.

note.en: Al-Tusi relays from Abu Said al-Khudri, Abu Wahb and al-Zajjaj that People of the Book left the Prophet claiming he had brought them what they already knew, and Muslims praised them for it [16].

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: نزلت في المنافقين الذين يحبون أن يحمدوا على غير فعل

text.en: It came down about the hypocrites, who love to be praised for what they have not done.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: قوله { ولا تحسبنهم بمفازة من العذاب } يقول ببعيد من العذاب { ولهم عذاب أليم }.
narrations.chain: in the narration of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: "Do not suppose them saved from punishment" means: far off from the punishment. "And there is a painful punishment for them."

perspectives.en: Both traditions read the charge "why did you kill them" as fastening an old crime on a later generation, but they apply the principle in opposite directions. Al-Qurtubi reports that when a man spoke well of the killing of Uthman in al-Shabi's presence, al-Shabi told him he had shared in his blood, making consent to a killing a killing [45]. The reports gathered in al-Burhan turn the same principle on those who defend the killers of the Imams: al-Sadiq cursed the Murjia, who claim that those who killed us were believers, so their clothes are stained with our blood until the Day of Resurrection [25].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وقد استدل بعضهم بالآية على ثبوت البرزخ لدلالتها على سبق بعض الإعطاء وأن الذي في يوم القيامة هو الإعطاء الكامل وهو استدلال حسن

sources.gloss: Some have argued from the verse for the establishing of the intermediate state, since it indicates that some giving comes earlier and that what falls on the Day of Resurrection is the full giving; and it is a good argument.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قالت اليهود إن الله فقير يستقرض منا ونحن أغنياء وقائلـه حيي بن أخطب عن الحسن ومجاهد

sources.gloss: The Jews said: Allah is poor, He asks a loan of us, and we are rich. The one who said it was Hayy ibn Akhtab, from al-Hasan and Mujahid.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل إن الله أمر بني إسرائيل في التوراة من جاءكم يزعم أنه نبيّ فلا تصدقوه حتى يأتي بقربان تأكلـه النار حتى يأتيكم عيسى ومحمد فإذا أتياكم فآمنوا بهما بغير قربان

sources.gloss: It is said that Allah commanded the Children of Israel in the Torah: whoever comes to you claiming to be a prophet, do not believe him until he brings an offering consumed by fire, until Isa and Muhammad come to you; and when they come, believe in them without an offering.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على أن أقلّ نعيم من الآخرة خير من نعيم الدنيا بأسره

sources.gloss: The verse indicates that the least bliss of the hereafter is better than the bliss of this world entire.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi
