excerpt.text: نزلت الآية في كعب بن الأشرف وكان يهجو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين ويحرّض المشركين عليهم

sources.gloss: The verse came down about Kab ibn al-Ashraf, who used to lampoon the Prophet and the believers and incite the polytheists against them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ودلَّت الآية على وجوب إظهار الحق وتحريم كتمانِه فيدخل فيه بيان الدين والأَحكام والفتاوى والشهادات

sources.gloss: The verse establishes the obligation of making the truth manifest and the prohibition of concealing it, and this takes in the explaining of religion, rulings, verdicts and testimony.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على أن الرضا بقبيح الفعل يجري مجراه في عظم الجرم

sources.gloss: The verse indicates that being pleased with a foul deed runs the course of that deed in the enormity of the crime.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفيها دلالة على بطلان مذهب المجبرة، لأنها تدل على أنه لو وقع العقاب من غير جرم سلف من العبد، لكان ظلماً

sources.gloss: In it is an indication of the falsity of the doctrine of the determinists, since it shows that were punishment to fall without a crime already committed by the servant, it would be injustice.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وهذه الآية فيها تسلية للنبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) عما كان يصيبه من الأذى من اليهود وأهل الشرك بتكذيبهم إياه

sources.gloss: This verse holds consolation for the Prophet regarding the injury that reached him from the Jews and the people of idolatry through their denial of him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال أبو سعيد الخدري، وأبو وهب، والزجاج: المعني بهذه الآية قوم من أهل الكتاب دخلوا على النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) وخرجوا من عنده، فذكروا لمن كان رآهم في ذلك الوقت أن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قد أتاهم باشياء قد عرفوها، فحمدهم من شاهدهم من المسلمين على ذلك

sources.gloss: Abu Said al-Khudri, Abu Wahb and al-Zajjaj said: what is meant by this verse is a group of the People of the Book who came in to the Prophet and left him, then told those who had seen them at the time that the Prophet had brought them things they already knew, and the Muslims who witnessed it praised them for that.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفى الآية تكذيب لمن قال: { إن الله فقير ونحن أغنياء } لأن من ملك ما في السماوات والارض لا يكون فقيراً

sources.gloss: In the verse is a belying of those who said, "Allah is poor and we are rich," for one who owns what is in the heavens and the earth is not poor.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: (والزبر) وهي كتب الأنبياء بالنبوة { والكتاب المنير } الحلال والحرام

sources.gloss: "Holy writs": these are the books of the prophets carrying prophethood. "An illuminating scripture": the lawful and the unlawful.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وذلك أن الله أخذ ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب في محمد لتبيننه للناس إذا خرج ولا يكتمونه

sources.gloss: That is because Allah took the covenant of those given the Book concerning Muhammad, that they would explain him to the people when he came forth and not conceal him.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: نزلت في المنافقين الذين يحبون أن يحمدوا على غير فعل

sources.gloss: It came down about the hypocrites, who love to be praised for what they have not done.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و الله ما رأوا الله فيعلمون أنه فقير، و لكنهم رأوا أولياء الله فقراء

sources.gloss: By Allah, they did not see Allah so as to know that He is poor; rather they saw the friends of Allah poor.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن هؤلاء زعموا أن الذين قتلونا كانوا مؤمنين، فثيابهم ملطخة بدمائنا إلى يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: These men claim that those who killed us were believers, so their clothes are stained with our blood until the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لوددت أني تركت فكلمت الناس ثلاثا، ثم قضى الله تعالى في ما أحب، و لكن عزمة من الله أن نصبر

sources.gloss: I would have loved to be left free to speak to the people for three days, and then for Allah to decree concerning me what He loves. But it is a resolve from Allah that we be patient.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أَمَا والله ما قتلوهم بأسيافهم ولكن أذاعوا أمرهم وأفشوا عليهم فقتلوا

sources.gloss: By Allah, they did not kill them with their swords; they broadcast their affair and exposed them, and so they were killed.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وحسَّن رجل عند الشعبي قتْل عثمان رضي الله عنه فقال له الشعبي. شَرِكَت في دمه. فجعل الرضا بالقتل قتْلا

sources.gloss: A man spoke well of the killing of Uthman in al-Shabi's presence, and al-Shabi said to him: you have shared in his blood. So he made being pleased with a killing a killing.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: قُلْتُ: يا رَبِّ اَيَمُوتُ الخَلائِقُ كُلُّهُم وَيَبقَى المَلائِكَةُ؟ فَنَزَلَت (كلُّ نَفسِ ذائِقَةُ المَوتِ ثُمَّ إِلَينا ترجَعُونَ)

sources.gloss: I said: my Lord, will all creatures die and the angels remain? Then was revealed, "Every soul shall taste death, then to Us you shall be brought back."

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: لَمَّا قُبِضَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ص جَاءَ الْخَضِرُ ع فَوَقَفَ عَلَى بَابِ الْبَيْتِ

sources.gloss: When the Messenger of Allah was taken, al-Khidr came and stood at the door of the house.

essay.en:
The surah closes by turning the reader back to what stands in plain sight. Tabatabai reads these verses as a summary of everything the surah has said about the believers, the polytheists and the People of the Book: the righteous remember God, reflect on His signs, seek refuge from the Fire and ask forgiveness, and God answers them [1]. Tusi finds in the opening verse a proof that looking and reasoning are obligatory, and a rebuttal of those who hold that faith can only come by imitation and report [8].

The signs are the heavens, the earth and the turning of night into day, and those who read them remember God standing, sitting, and lying on their sides. Their reflection ends in a verdict: 'Our Lord, You have not created this in vain.' Tusi notes that the demonstrative is singular because what is meant is the creation taken as one work [9]. Since nothing is purposeless, a reckoning must follow, and the petitions begin: shelter from the Fire, forgiveness, death among the pious, and the promise given through the apostles. Who the summoner was is disputed: Tusi records that al-Qurazi and Qatada made it the Quran, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd the Messenger [11], and al-Qummi glosses him as the Messenger calling to faith [18].

'Then their Lord answered them.' Tabrisi reports that Umm Salama asked why men are named in the emigration and not women, and this verse came down [4]. Then the two futures are set side by side. When some Muslims saw the polytheists trading in comfort and said that God's enemies live at ease while we die of hunger, Tabrisi reports, the warning against their bustle was revealed [5]. The Book's own people are not excluded: Tabrisi reports that verse 199 came down when the Prophet prayed over the Negus [6], while Tusi prefers Mujahid's reading, that it covers everyone of the People of the Book who accepted Islam [16]. The last verse draws the conclusion: patience, endurance shared, and a binding of the community's powers and acts across the whole of its religious life [2].

note.en: Tabrisi reports that the Imams commanded reciting these five verses on rising at night for prayer, and that the Prophet, rising at night, would use the siwak, look at the sky, and recite them [3].

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: ويل لمن لاكها بين فكّيه ولم يتأمل ما فيها

text.en: Woe to one who chews these verses between his jaws and does not ponder what is in them.

narrations.speaker: Imam Musa ibn Jafar
narrations.arabic: يا هشام، إن الله تبارك و تعالى بشر أهل العقل و الفهم في كتابه … يا هشام، إن لكل شيء دليلا، و دليل العقل التفكر، و دليل التفكر الصمت
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu Abdullah al-Ashari, from some of our companions, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam

text.en: O Hisham, God gave good news to the people of intellect and understanding in His Book. Everything has a proof; the proof of the intellect is reflection, and the proof of reflection is silence.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألت أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) عما يروي الناس: أن تفكر ساعة خير من قيام ليلة، قلت: كيف يتفكر؟ … يمر بالخربة أو بالدار، فيقول: أين ساكنوك، أين بانوك، ما لك لا تتكلمين؟
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Aban, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal

text.en: I asked him about what people relate, that an hour of reflection is better than a night in prayer, and how one reflects. He said: he passes by a ruin or a house and says, where are those who dwelt in you, where are those who built you, why do you not speak?

note.en: Tusi gives two readings: that they remember God in every state, and that they pray as they are able in health and sickness, which he says our own narrations report; he finds no conflict between them [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الصَّحِيحُ يُصَلِّي قَائِماً وَقُعُوداً الْمَرِيضُ يُصَلِّي جَالِساً وَعَلى‏ جُنُوبِهِمْ الَّذِي يَكُونُ أَضْعَفَ مِنَ الْمَرِيضِ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي جَالِساً.
narrations.chain: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Jafar

text.en: A healthy man prays standing and sitting. A sick man prays seated. And 'lying on their sides' is the one who is weaker than the sick man who prays seated.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: لا يزال المؤمن في صلاة ما كان في ذكر الله عز وجل قائما كان أو جالسا أو مضطجعا
narrations.chain: Al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad al-Balkhi al-Warraq, from Muhammad ibn Hammam al-Iskafi, from Abdullah ibn Jafar al-Himyari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir

text.en: The believer remains in prayer as long as he is in the remembrance of God, whether standing, sitting or lying down.

note.en: On 'the wrongdoers will have no helpers', Tusi holds that this does not conflict with intercession for those guilty of grave sins, since intercession is petition and humility before God, not the force of a helper [10].
Al-Qummi reads 'those who migrated and were expelled from their homes' as Amir al-Muminin, Salman and Abu Dharr, when he was driven out [19].
Al-Qummi identifies them as a people of the Jews and the Christians who entered Islam, among them the Negus and his companions [21].

Tabrisi records that Ali read 'close your ranks' as awaiting one prayer after another, since frontier duty did not yet exist, and al-Baqir as patience in calamities and standing firm against the enemy [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: اصبروا على الفرائض، و صابروا على المصائب، و رابطوا على الأئمة
narrations.chain: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Safatij, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Be patient in the obligations, endure the calamities, and keep bound to the Imams.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: اصبروا على أداء الفرائض، و صابروا عدوكم، و رابطوا إمامكم المنتظر
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandanaiji, from Ubaydallah ibn Musa al-Abbasi, from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Burayd ibn Muawiya al-Ijli, from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir

text.en: Be patient in performing the obligations, endure against your enemy, and keep bound to your awaited Imam.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إذا كان يوم القيامة ينادي مناد أين الصابرون؟ فيقوم فئام من الناس ثم ينادي أين المتصبرون، فيقوم فئام من الناس، قلت جعلت فداك وما الصابرون؟ قال على أداء الفرايض والمتصبرون على اجتناب المحارم
narrations.chain: His father, from al-Hasan ibn Khalid, from al-Rida

text.en: When the Day of Resurrection comes a caller will call: where are the patient? A company of people will rise. Then he will call: where are those who persevered? A company will rise. I said: what are the patient? He said: upon performing the obligations; and those who persevered, upon avoiding what is forbidden.

perspectives.en: The closing command turns on 'rabitu'. Al-Tabari records al-Hasan reading it as being patient in one's religion, enduring against the disbelievers and standing guard over the polytheists, and others as awaiting one prayer after another [38]. Suyuti has Abu Hurayra say there was no frontier campaign in the Prophet's day, and Jabir report the Prophet naming full ablution in hardship, many steps to the mosques and awaiting prayer after prayer as the ribat [58]. Shia narrations keep those senses and add a third: al-Baqir told Burayd ibn Muawiya to be patient in the obligations, endure against the enemy, and keep bound to the awaited Imam [25].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الآيات بمنزلة تلخيص ما تقدم من بيان حال المؤمنين والمشركين وأهل الكتاب في هذه السورة

sources.gloss: The verses are like a summary of what has come before in this surah on the state of the believers, the polytheists and the People of the Book.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: قوله تعالى { ورابطوا } أعم معنى من المصابرة وهي إيجاد الجماعة الارتباط بين قواهم وأفعالهم في جميع شؤون حياتهم الدينية

sources.gloss: 'And close your ranks' is wider in meaning than musabara: it is a community's forging of a bond between their powers and their acts in every part of their religious life.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وورد عن الأئمة من آل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم الأمر بقراءة هذه الآيات الخمس وقت القيام بالليل للصلاة وفي الضجعة بعد ركعتي الفجر

sources.gloss: It has come from the Imams of the family of Muhammad that these five verses be recited at the time of rising by night for prayer, and in the lying down after the two units of dawn.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: روي أنّ أم سلمة قالت يا رسول الله ما بال الرجال يذكرون في الـهجرة دون النساء فأنزل الله هذه الآية

sources.gloss: It is related that Umm Salama said: Messenger of God, why are the men mentioned in the emigration and not the women? So God sent down this verse.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في مشركي العرب وكانوا يتجرون ويتنعمون بها فقال بعض المسلمين إن أعداء الله في العيش الرخيّ وقد هلكنا من الجوع فنزلت الآية

sources.gloss: It was revealed about the Arab polytheists, who used to trade and take their comfort in it, so that some of the Muslims said: the enemies of God are in easy living while we have perished of hunger. So the verse came down.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في النجاشي ملك الحبشة واسمه أصحمة وهو بالعربية عطية

sources.gloss: It was revealed about the Negus, king of Abyssinia, whose name was Ashama, which in Arabic is Atiyya.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل إن معنى رابطوا أي رابطوا الصلوات ومعناه انتظروها واحدة بعد واحدة لأن المرابطة لم تكن حينئذ روي ذلك عن علي بن أبي طالب … وروي عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع أنه قال: معناه اصبروا على المصائب وصابروا على عدوكم ورابطوا عدوكم

sources.gloss: It is said that 'rabitu' means keep to the prayers, that is, await them one after another, since standing guard did not exist at that time; this is related from Ali ibn Abi Talib. ... And it is related from Abu Jafar al-Baqir that he said: it means be patient over calamities, endure against your enemy, and stand guard against your enemy.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: في هذه الآية دلالة على وجوب النظر والفكر، والاعتبار بما يشاهد من الخلق والاستدلال على الله تعالى، ومدح لمن كانت صفته هذه، ورد على من أنكر وجوب ذلك، وزعم أن الايمان لا يكون إلا تقليداً وبالخبر

sources.gloss: In this verse is a proof of the obligation of looking and reflecting, of taking a lesson from the creation one observes and reasoning from it to God, and praise for whoever is of this description, and a refutation of one who denied that this is obligatory and claimed that faith can only be by imitation and by report.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: انما قال هذا ولم يقل هذه ولا هؤلاء، لأنه أراد به الخلق كأنه قال ما خلقت هذا الخلق باطلا

sources.gloss: He said 'this' and not 'these', because He meant by it the creation, as though He said: You did not create this creation in vain.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ولا ينافي ذلك الشفاعة في أهل الكبائر لأن الشفاعة هي مسألة وخضوع وضرع إلى الله تعالى، وليست من النصرة في شيء

sources.gloss: That does not conflict with intercession for those guilty of grave sins, for intercession is petition, humility and pleading before God, and is nothing of the nature of a helper's aid.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: واختلفوا فيمن المنادي ها هنا، فقال محمد بن كعب القرظي وقتادة: هو القرآن. وقال ابن جريج وابن زيد: هو رسول الله

sources.gloss: They differed over who the summoner is here. Muhammad ibn Kab al-Qurazi and Qatada said: it is the Quran. Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: it is the Messenger of God.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال مجاهد: إنها نزلت في كل من أسلم من أهل الكتاب من اليهود والنصارى وهو أولى، لأنه عموم الآية

sources.gloss: Mujahid said: it was revealed about everyone of the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, who accepted Islam; and this is preferable, because of the generality of the verse.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني رسول الله ينادي إلى الإِيمان

sources.gloss: That is, the Messenger of God calling to faith.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني أمير المؤمنين وسلمان وأبا ذر حين أخرج

sources.gloss: That is, Amir al-Muminin, Salman and Abu Dharr, when he was driven out.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فهم قوم من اليهود والنصارى دخلوا في الإِسلام، منهم النجاشي وأصحابه

sources.gloss: They are a people of the Jews and the Christians who entered Islam, among them the Negus and his companions.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: إذا كان يوم القيامة ينادي مناد أين الصابرون؟ فيقوم فئام من الناس ثم ينادي أين المتصبرون، فيقوم فئام من الناس، قلت جعلت فداك وما الصابرون؟ قال على أداء الفرايض والمتصبرون على اجتناب المحارم

sources.gloss: When the Day of Resurrection comes a caller will call: where are the patient? ... upon performing the obligations; and those who persevered, upon avoiding what is forbidden.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يا هشام، إن لكل شيء دليلا، و دليل العقل التفكر، و دليل التفكر الصمت

sources.gloss: O Hisham, everything has a proof; the proof of the intellect is reflection, and the proof of reflection is silence.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: اصبروا على أداء الفرائض، و صابروا عدوكم، و رابطوا إمامكم المنتظر

sources.gloss: Be patient in performing the obligations, endure against your enemy, and keep bound to your awaited Imam.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: أمرهم أن يصبروا علـى دينهم، ولا يدعوه لشدّة ولا رخاء، ولا سرّاء ولا ضرّاء، وأمرهم أن يصابروا الكفـار، وأن يرابطوا الـمشركين

sources.gloss: He commanded them to be patient in their religion and not abandon it for hardship or ease, for joy or affliction, and commanded them to endure against the disbelievers and to stand guard over the polytheists.

sources.author: Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti

excerpt.text: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: لم يكن في زمان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم غزو يرابط فيه ولكن انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

sources.gloss: I heard Abu Hurayra say: in the time of the Prophet there was no campaign in which one stood guard, but rather the awaiting of one prayer after another.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: الصَّحِيحُ يُصَلِّي قَائِماً وَقُعُوداً الْمَرِيضُ يُصَلِّي جَالِساً وَعَلى‏ جُنُوبِهِمْ الَّذِي يَكُونُ أَضْعَفَ مِنَ الْمَرِيضِ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي جَالِساً.

sources.gloss: A healthy man prays standing and sitting, a sick man prays seated, and 'on their sides' is the one who is weaker than the sick man who prays seated.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. muhammad al-mufid

excerpt.text: لا يزال المؤمن في صلاة ما كان في ذكر الله عز وجل قائما كان أو جالسا أو مضطجعا

sources.gloss: The believer remains in prayer as long as he is in the remembrance of God, standing, sitting or lying down.
